- No money arm (owner, 2026-11-15): one is added to `Cost` with the first metered vendor. Rejected
  now: an arm nothing produces is a branch nothing reaches.

**`robots`: one row per answered robots.txt fetch (user_version 2, `MIGRATIONS[1]`).**

| column | notes |
|---|---|
| `attempt_id` | primary key and foreign key to the fetch's `attempts` row, `source` `robots` (§10) |
| `host` | the lowercased hosts-file host the fetch asked |
| `answer` | `present` (HTTP 200) \| `absent` (HTTP 404), `CHECK`ed; any other status files no row (§11.2) |
| `blob` | the body as received, foreign key to `blobs`, for a `present` row closed before user_version 6; NULL on every row from user_version 6, whose body is named by its `payloads` row alone (§3.9) |

- One home for a robots body (builder default 2026-11-16, §10): the `payloads` row from user_version 6, `robots.blob` before it; readers take `COALESCE(robots.blob, payloads.raw_blob)` for a `present` row (`store::ROBOTS_BODY`). The `answer` column decides `present` or `absent`, because a 404's body is a payload too.
  - `a_robots_body_is_read_from_robots_blob_before_user_version_six_and_from_payloads_after`: a hand-written pre-6 row, a row written by `record_robots` (its `robots.blob` NULL) and a `present` row naming neither, `StoreError::RobotsBodyUnlinked` (mutations 2026-11-16: `r.blob` alone: red; `p.raw_blob` alone: red; `record_robots` writing `robots.blob` again: red).
  - a v5 store, read by `collect`'s check before its lease migrates it, has no `payloads` and is read through `robots.blob` alone: `a_v5_store_s_robots_row_is_read_without_the_payloads_table` (mutation 2026-11-16, `payloads` assumed present: red).
- One door, `Committer::record_robots(AttemptReceipt, host, RobotsAnswer, &Payload, at)`: `record`'s checks
  (opened here, closed here, an abandoned attempt carries nothing, a replay must be the same row,
  else `StoreError::RobotsReplayDiffers` naming both rows, and the same payload row, else `StoreError::ReplayWithDifferentPayload`, a comparison no robots test reaches, unguarded), then the `Answered` and `Finalised` events, the blob's index row, the `payloads` row and the `robots` row in one
  transaction: `a_robots_row_and_its_attempt_events_commit_in_one_transaction` (mutation
  2026-11-15, the insert moved after `COMMIT`: red);
  `a_robots_replay_naming_another_host_or_answer_is_refused` (mutation 2026-11-15, the replay
  comparison skipped: red). A `Present` digest other than the payload's is `StoreError::RobotsAnswerIsNotItsPayload`, before any write: `a_robots_answer_naming_another_blob_than_its_payload_is_refused` (mutation 2026-11-16, the check skipped: red).
- Producer: `newsvault robots refresh` (§11.2). Reader: `store::RobotsLedger::newest_robots`,
  read-only, the newest answered fetch of a host by `closed_at` then `attempt_id`; called by
  `collect`'s robots check (§8 row R4, robots clause).

**`deferred`: one row per request a run did not ask (user_version 13, `MIGRATIONS[12]`, S7-D4, 2026-11-18; keyed at user_version 14, `MIGRATIONS[13]`, S7-D5; `listed_by` at user_version 15, `MIGRATIONS[14]`, §8 row R22).**

| column | notes |
|---|---|
| `deferred_id` | since user_version 14: `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, each v13 row's rowid carried by the rebuild (`a_v13_store_keeps_every_v13_column_of_every_row`); the key a `deferred_closed` row names. Rejected: naming a row by its plain rowid; `VACUUM` may renumber the rowids of a table with no `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (SQLite docs, VACUUM) |
| `run_id`, `source`, `target_window` | the run that did not ask, and the request's source and window |
| `host` | the url's `HostKey` (`host_of`, the key the queue's lanes and `Wire`'s pace use); NULL for a url it cannot key |
| `url`, `phase`, `listed_date` | the request as the queue held it; `phase` `CHECK`ed `index` \| `document`; `follow_up_cap` defers `document` only (a counted follow-up, §11.2's cap bullet); a stopped lane defers both (PRN's sitemap page behind its held RSS, `a_held_host_past_the_deadline_is_stopped_with_its_lane_while_the_other_hosts_are_asked`) |
| `story_id` | `Provider::story_of` for a `Document` request, the rule `attempt_once` opens an attempt under; NULL for an `Index` request and a follow-up that names no story |
| `reason` | `run_deadline` \| `host_held` \| `follow_up_cap`, `CHECK`ed; `news_provider::DeferReason`, three arms, since 2026-11-18 (§11.5 step 7 PR 3); the split of the first two is §11.5 step 7's condition A bullets |
| `deferred_at` | the driver's clock when the queue reached the request, one instant for a whole stopped lane; the age S7-D5's 24 h expiry reads (`deferred_closed`, below) |
| `listed_by` | since user_version 15: the queued request's `attempts.listed_by` (above), so the attempt a later run asks it under names the index attempt that first listed it; NULL where the request's is |

- Not an attempt row: no call was made, so §8 row R16's one attempt row per HTTP call holds (S7-D4's rejected alternative).
- No natural key: a url the queue reaches twice in one run and defers twice is two rows, each a fact; the carry reads them as one item (below).
- Not stored: the instant the pace would have sent the request at. It is the envelope's `deferred[].go_at`, set on the one row whose reservation came back past the deadline and null on the rest of its lane and on `follow_up_cap` rows.
- Producers, both in `news_provider::collect`, each through `Archive::record_deferred` to `Committer::record_deferred`, one `INSERT` before the next request; a refused write aborts the run (`CollectError::Archive`):
  - `follow_up_cap`: `HostQueue::pop` hands back `Popped::Defer`.
  - `run_deadline`, `host_held`: `Exchange::reserve` answers `Reservation::PastDeadline`; that request and every request left in its host's lane (`HostQueue::stop`) are deferred under one reason.
- Readers: `ledger`'s source-row `deferred` (one count per reason, by the run's day, under `--source` too; its human line `deferred_run_deadline`, `deferred_host_held`, `deferred_follow_up_cap`), the collect envelope's `deferred[]` and `per_source[].deferred`, and its `deferred` human line, one count per reason; and since 2026-11-18 the carry, which reads its open `document` rows (`deferred_closed`, below).
- Tests: `services/newsvault/tests/open_web_collect.rs::the_301st_follow_up_is_deferred_recorded_and_never_sent_and_the_run_exits_8` (every column, envelope, human line, ledger); `a_run_of_exactly_300_follow_ups_asks_every_one_and_defers_none`; `a_walked_poll_past_the_cap_sends_every_walk_id_and_defers_listed_releases_only` (walk ids never deferred by the cap; a deferral takes no ordinal, so later `attempt_id`s stay dense); `deferred_requests_open_no_attempt_and_every_reader_counts_each_reason_apart` (3 `run_deadline`, 4 `host_held`, 0 `follow_up_cap` in the envelope, both human lines and the ledger); `services/newsvault/tests/ledger.rs::deferred_rows_are_counted_per_reason_for_the_source_and_day_of_their_run`; migration: §8 row M1. Mutations: §11.5 step 7 PRs 2 and 3.

**`deferred_closed`: one row per `deferred` row the carry closed (user_version 14, `MIGRATIONS[13]`, S7-D5, 2026-11-18).**

| column | notes |
|---|---|
| `deferred_id` | primary key and foreign key to `deferred`: a row is closed once, never updated; a second close is refused by the key and nothing of that call is kept (`Committer::close_deferred`, one transaction) |
| `run_id` | the run that closed it |
| `closed_as` | `answered` \| `held` \| `expired`, `CHECK`ed; `news_provider::Closing::name`, three arms |
| `attempt_id` | foreign key to `attempts`: the run's first attempt that asked the item's url or story; set exactly when `answered` (a table `CHECK`) |
| `closed_at` | the driver's clock at the close |

- The reader: `Committer::open_deferred`, at the start of `news_provider::collect`, after the startup sweep and inside the lease, before the first request. It reads the source's `document` rows no `deferred_closed` row names, oldest `deferred_at` first; one url's rows are one carried item.
- Each item, in that order:
  - its story is in `Archive::held_story_ids`: closed `held`, not asked;
  - else its oldest open row is 24 h old or older by the run's clock at its start (`CARRY_LIMIT`, inclusive): not carried, and decided once the queue is empty (below); the age stays the start's even when the clock passes 24 h during the run (`age_is_read_at_the_runs_start_and_a_row_closes_at_its_attempts_clock`);
  - else `Provider::carried` rebuilds the request from `url`, `listed_date` and the oldest row's `target_window`, and takes the oldest row's `listed_by`, under this run's hosts file and extraction version (owner decision 2026-11-18, answer c); it goes into its host's lane behind every request of this run on that host: the planned index, the follow-ups it lists, the next sitemap page, walk ids and retries (`HostQueue::carry`, S7-D5 as amended 2026-11-19); its story joins `issued`, so an index of the run listing it again drops it and it stays carried, asked once (`a_relisted_carried_story_stays_carried_and_is_not_issued_twice`);
  - else (a url off an admitted host, keying no story, or one the pinned robots now disallow; every `edgar-press` row, whose `carried` is `None`) it is not carried (`a_young_item_the_provider_cannot_rebuild_is_not_asked_and_stays_open`).
- Once the queue is empty, each item not carried and not closed (`close_uncarried`): closed `answered` by the run's first attempt that asked its url or its story, carried or not; else `expired` when over 24 h; else left open for the next run. Reason (PR #53 review F1, 2026-11-18): closed `expired` at the start, an over-age walk id the run's own walk listed again was asked in the same run while the ledger and `--check` said "never asked" (`an_over_age_item_the_runs_own_index_lists_again_is_asked_and_closed_answered`: one row with no story matched by url, one under another spelling matched by story). Rejected: putting an over-age story in `issued`; the run's index would then drop a story it lists, a "did not look" with no row.
- A carried request is closed `answered` by its first attempt, whatever the verdict, with `closed_at` the clock right after that attempt; a retry after a transient failure closes nothing.
- A carried request deferred again (cap or deadline) is a new `deferred` row, and its older rows stay open, so the next run carries one item over every row and ages it from the oldest. Rejected: closing the older row on a re-deferral; the item's age would restart at each run and a host held for days would carry it forever.
- Counted against S7-D6's cap when it is no walk id (`Provider::is_walk_id`), at `pop` like any follow-up; a walk id stays outside it (S7-D6's exception). Rejected: carried items outside the cap; a run could then ask 300 new follow-ups plus every carried one, and the cap would bound nothing.
- `index` rows are never carried and never closed (owner decision 2026-11-18, PR #52 answer 4): the next run asks its indexes anyway, and the open row stays the "not looked" record. Rejected: closing them `superseded`; a fourth name with no reader, and a closed row would read as looked at.
- Readers: the collect envelope's `carried[]` (`source`, `target_window`, `host`, `url`, `story_id`, `deferred_ids`, `first_deferred_at`, `queued`, `closed_as`, `attempt_id`) and `per_source[].carried` (`queued`, `answered`, `held`, `expired`, one per item), additive within `newsvault.collect/2`, and its `carried` human line; `ledger`'s source-row `carried` (`answered`, `held`, `expired`, one per row, on the day of the closing run, under `--source` too, its human line `carried_answered`, `carried_held`, `carried_expired`); `ledger --check`'s `deferred_expired` finding for any expired count (S7-D8); the hourly watchdog's `newsvault_carried_expired` and its `NewsvaultDeferredExpired` alert (§11.5 step 7 PR 6).
- Tests, `services/newsvault/tests/open_web_collect.rs`: `deferred_walk_ids_are_carried_behind_their_lanes_index_and_closed_answered`; `a_carried_item_whose_story_the_store_holds_is_closed_held_and_not_asked`; `a_deferred_item_is_carried_at_23_59_59_and_closed_expired_at_24_hours` (the ledger count and the finding too); `a_carried_request_deferred_again_keeps_its_rows_open_and_ages_from_its_first`; `deferred_index_requests_are_never_carried_or_closed`; `a_carried_follow_up_counts_against_the_cap_and_a_carried_walk_id_does_not`; `an_over_age_item_the_runs_own_index_lists_again_is_asked_and_closed_answered`; `a_young_item_the_provider_cannot_rebuild_is_not_asked_and_stays_open`; `age_is_read_at_the_runs_start_and_a_row_closes_at_its_attempts_clock`; `a_relisted_carried_story_stays_carried_and_is_not_issued_twice`. Also `news_provider::collect::tests::a_lane_asks_its_planned_index_then_new_follow_ups_then_carried_requests`, `…::carried_requests_follow_their_lanes_index_and_only_counted_ones_spend_the_cap`, `…::the_cap_is_spent_on_new_follow_ups_before_carried_ones`, `…::a_lane_out_of_fresh_requests_asks_its_carried_one_in_its_own_turn`, `…::a_stopped_lane_defers_its_carried_requests_too` and `…::a_carried_request_on_a_host_with_no_lane_opens_one_and_is_asked`, `open-web-feed`'s `a_deferred_document_is_rebuilt_as_its_request_and_a_walk_id_is_known_by_its_url`, `edgar-press`'s `edgar_press_carries_no_deferred_document`, `ledger.rs::closed_deferred_rows_are_counted_per_closing_and_an_expired_one_is_a_finding` (1 answered, 2 held, 3 expired). Migration: §8 row M1. Mutations: §11.5 step 7 PR 5.
- Unguarded: an `edgar-press` row is never carried, so it reaches only `expired`; no test runs an EDGAR collect over an open row.

- `collapsed` is designed as its own outcome: a payload that shrank to a fraction of what the store
  already holds is a degraded fetch, not a quieter world, and a throttled success looks exactly like
  a quiet day.
- Not built: `OutcomeKind` has no such arm, so a collapse-shaped payload is filed `ok`
  (`decide_cannot_return_collapsed_until_a_floor_with_our_own_construction_exists`).
- Its floor waits for our own construction: `baseline_ratio` (`Baseline.ratio` in
  `news-provider/src/ledger.rs`) is written on every decided attempt, NULL when the trailing median
  is 0 (which includes no prior `ok` attempt), so the floor can be picked from real runs.

### 3.3 `RuleSet` — what `derive` is a function of

- A hashed, versioned file, the only place these choices exist. Rejected: constants in code, which cannot be diffed, tested or attributed (§2 `rule_version`).
- Design: no `rules/1` file and no reader exist (`rg '"rules/1"'` outside `docs/`, 2026-11-15; the one rules file in the tree is `edgar-press.rules/1`, extraction rules digested as `extract_rules_version`); `derive` has no code (§3.0).

| group | contents |
|---|---|
| `entity_rules` | corporate-suffix list (complete, no ellipsis), case policy per token count, minimum core length, and three gazetteers: generic name components, non-companies, places |
| `salience_rule` | six keys, each a literal, never an expression: `counting_unit` (**memo D-8's, open**), `window_sessions`, `baseline_sessions`, `order_statistic`, `floor` (counted in `counting_unit`, so **memo D-8's too**), `tie_rule`. **Salience** is how often a counterparty's **core** — the name token a match is made on — occurs in the window ending at T, in `counting_unit`; the core is salient when that count is at or above `floor` and at or above the `order_statistic` of its own baseline |
| `panel_rule` | `presence`: which (ticker, session) rows exist, and nothing else — all `derive` decides about the panel's shape. Winsorisation and market adjustment: the statistics tier's, below |

- Each gazetteer entry is a line in a file and therefore a diff.
- Motivating case: a hand-written gazetteer removed `Premier`, a real company and counterparty, and nothing recorded the error because the list lived inside a script.

**The file, what `rule_version` digests, and the two keys still blank.**

- One JSON object, keys sorted, LF endings, one trailing newline.
- `rule_version` is sha256 of those bytes as committed (`canon::FileDigest::of`), so a whitespace edit is a new version: wrong in the safe direction, and no second canonicalisation.
- Gazetteers and the calendar are their own files (§2), named by path and digest so one `rule_version` still covers the set.
- The two `null`s are memo D-8's and only memo D-8's; every other value is the example's own, the shape being what is contracted:

```json
{"schema": "rules/1",
 "entity_rules": {"suffixes": "suffixes.txt@sha256:3f2a…", "min_core_chars": 4, "case_policy": {"1": "exact", "2+": "fold"}},
 "salience_rule": {"counting_unit": null, "window_sessions": 1, "baseline_sessions": 60, "order_statistic": "q90", "floor": null, "tie_rule": "name_ascending_bytes"},
 "panel_rule": {"presence": "close_on_session_and_next"}}
```

**Where the winsorisation cuts and the market adjustment live.**

- Not in the rule set: both act on a return and §3.10.1's panel carries none.
- Today both are inline in `probes/panel_power.py`: the session cross-sectional mean subtracted (`:87`) and the 1st/99th percentile clip (`:88`–`:89`), beside its floors, alpha, draw counts and seed (`:52`–`:55`).
- Their home is that tier's own hashed params file; its digest — `params_version`, named here and nowhere else — goes beside every power number.

### 3.4 `Panel` — `derive` to `propose`, and to the statistics tier

- An Arrow file plus a manifest, and not a call: the panel outlives the process (§4).
- The data file is §3.10.1.
- **The manifest's field list is not here**: `panel-contract schema --format=json` names every field, its `need` (always required or not) and its `why`. Cost: a reader runs a binary. Rejected: a copy here, free to over-promise or under-report against the checker.
- `panel.manifest/2` since 2026-11-22 (owner decision 6a): `seq_high_water` is required beside `snapshot_id` as an integer of at least 1 (`Shape::SeqBound`: `snapshot.manifest/1` and `cut --through-seq` refuse 0), and `snapshot_id` must be canon's digest text form (`Shape::Digest`). A snapshot directory is kept outside the backup (§3.0), so the cited cut's bound would otherwise be lost with it. Both refuse a manifest version 1 admitted, hence the major version; no producer of version 1 existed (`derive` has no code).

**Why the field set exists**, which no field list carries.

- The predecessor's power at the 0.05 sd floor, α = 0.05, by construction, measured 2026-11-11 (memo §1.8, §1.9):

| construction | power |
|---|---|
| independent-rows formula | 88.2% |
| measured through the predecessor's own randomization procedure | 27.4% |
| same, on a corrected archive | 10.9% |

- The formula answered a different question and nothing could tell.
- Hence `rows` is **counted**, never multiplied: the predecessor's panel was `len(universe) * len(sessions)`, a rectangle wearing a count's clothes.
- `exchangeable_units` carries `count`, `unit`, `definition` (`check_units_shape` in `panel-contract/src/lib.rs`); `definition` because the unit's name alone does not say what made two exchangeable.
- A required field is half the fix; the other half, a consumer that **refuses** a panel lacking it, does not exist: `panel-contract` requires the field (§8 row R8) while the statistics code reads an ad-hoc `assign.json` + `meta.json` and counts its own units (row R9).

### 3.5 `ModelRequest` / `ModelResponse` — the only exit to a model (amended 2026-11-23)

- Built: `services/modelgate`, `decide` calls only, and one command, `modelgate shadow run` (§8 rows MG1 to MG14). `generate` is design, no code.
- Built, not installed: the image's second binary, the wrapper, the unit, the timer and four alerts ("The shadow run on the VPS" below; §8 rows MG15 to MG18).
- Built 2026-11-24, not installed, not run: `modelgate snapshot`, `modelgate verify`, the store's daily copy to Nextcloud and two alerts ("The store's daily copy" below; §8 row MG19).
- Nothing has been sent to a model: every test runs against a stub or a `127.0.0.1` listener. "Not verified", below, lists what the first paid call decides.

| request | notes |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `decide` (a decision model: typed questions, probabilities back) \| `generate` (a generative model: text and choice; design, no code) |
| `question_version` | `canon::digest::question_version` over the question document: its name, then each question in the document's order as id, type, instructions, option ids, option descriptions. Nothing sorted: a reordered or reworded document is another version (`a_reordered_option_list_or_question_list_is_another_question_version`). Replaces `prompt_version` |
| `model` | a dated build id, `<id>-YYYYMMDD` with a real date. An alias (a leading `~`, or no date suffix) is refused before any row or socket (`modelgate::model::ModelId`) |
| `state` | the text the model reads: a story's `body` from a snapshot (§3.0), cut at a character boundary to 13,000 JSON-escaped bytes (`STATE_BUDGET_BYTES`). `state_digest` is the sha256 of the text sent |
| `schema` | `decide`: question id to `noul` (yes/no) or `choice` (named options, each described). `generate`: text and choice. **No schema has a numeric or date type: a model cannot be asked for a price, a return, a magnitude, a count, a date or a threshold.** A `score` type (2 to 10 described levels, never a number) is design, no code |
| `request_format` | `modelgate.request/2` (2026-11-23): the JSON layout, the state budget, the 22,600-byte bound on the encoded questions (`MAX_QUESTIONS_BYTES`) and the 35,800-byte ceiling on the whole body (`REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES`: 36 bytes of layout + a 128-byte model id + the two budgets = 35,764). The two budgets are independent, so two documents read the same cut of one story (`two_documents_of_different_length_cut_one_body_at_the_same_point`). `modelgate.request/1` (16,500 and 30,000) named no stored row: nothing was sent under it. Rejected, keeping 30,000 by cutting the state: `ripple-shadow/1` is 22,399 bytes, which leaves a state of 7,437, and D17 already asks whether 13,000 is too little. Rejected, 20,000 for the questions: the document measured 19,627 bytes while its `cx_*` and `as_*` questions did not say whose act they ask about, and 20,790 once each does (2026-11-23). Rejected, 21,000 and a ceiling of 34,200, the bounds of earlier that day: the two `spillover_*` questions add 1,609 bytes to 20,790, and shortening the two repeated lead-ins (the `ev_*` one to "Is this reported of the company reported on?", the `kp_*` one to "On a senior change at the company reported on:") frees 297 of the 1,399 needed and takes "the text" out of 21 questions. Cost: the largest request grows from 29,664 to 35,764 bytes, so its worst case grows by 20.6%. The token and the three numbers are literals in `request::tests::the_format_token_and_its_three_budgets_are_the_ones_the_design_names`, so a budget moves only with that test and this row. What the ceiling no longer bounds: "Not verified", the size limit; decision D19 |
| `idempotency_key` | `canon::digest::model_request` over (kind, request_format, question_version, state_digest, model, repeat_index). No story field: two stories with one body share one request, and each gets its own `labels` row. An ANSWERED request is never sent again; a process killed between the send and the commit of `answered` and `finalised` pays once more |
| `repeat_index` | `decide`: 0 is the label; 1 and above repeat the same bytes and are instrument noise. `generate`: the draw index (design) |

| response | notes |
|---|---|
| `outcome` | `ok` (2xx, a JSON object, a non-empty `answers`) \| `empty` (2xx, a JSON object, no answer and no `error` member) \| `unparseable` (2xx, not a JSON object) \| `failed` (no 2xx, or a 2xx object with an `error` member and no answer) \| `abandoned` (the next run's sweep closed it). `collapsed` and `interrupted` have no producer here and are not values. A failed call and an empty one never arrive as one answer; memo §1.5 is that defect costing 37 of 1,672 companies. `ok` alone is a label. `empty` and `unparseable` are final (paid once, bytes kept, never asked again; decision D18) and the run that paid for one exits 8 `unusable_answer` |
| `raw` | the request body and the response body as received, each a file under its sha256. The response is on disk before the row that names it, whatever it parses to. **The bytes are the record**; every field below is a reading of them |
| `answers` | `decide`: per question a probability (`noul`) or a top option and `probabilities` over the caller's options. Not stored as rows: read from the response bytes when asked for, so a wrong guess about the vendor's shape costs nothing permanent. No span: a decision model returns none |
| `value`, `span` | `generate` only (design): the answer and a verified character range in the state |
| `confidence` | `decide`: not stored; a function of `probabilities`. `generate`: the model's own. Neither is thresholded without a measurement |
| `model_build` | the vendor's `model` string, stored raw beside the id sent. Whether they match is computed when read (`answered_by_another_id`), never at write time, and the answer is kept either way: it is unknown whether a dated request echoes its dated id |
| `cost` | the vendor's `usage.cost` as integer micro-USD, rounded up; never recomputed. A stated cost of 0 is read as no cost stated. Charged against three caps that refuse BEFORE the call (below) |

Structural, not advisory:

- **A model is never asked for a quantity of the world**: `QuestionKind` is `Noul` or `Choice`, the file parser refuses any other `type` and any unknown field, so a careless document cannot break the rule.
- **The one number that crosses the boundary is a probability over a caller-defined, versioned answer space**, from a `decide` call, stored with the build that produced it.
  - Why the rule changed (2026-11-23): without it a decision model can only return its top option, which discards the calibrated reading the owner chose the model for. A probability is a reading of the text by one pinned build, never a forecast.
  - Code owns every comparison against it. A threshold is written in this document before the first outcome is read.
  - Readings from two builds, two models or two question versions are never pooled.
- **A bracket condition never enters a prompt**: filtering by market capitalisation, date or threshold happens afterwards in code, where it can be tested.
- **The sign of an effect is never asked.** The model answers about the text; code maps class and circumstances to a sign from a table frozen before any return is read (not written yet for the issuer; for other companies it is the channel table of "ripple/2"). `issuer_effect` and `spillover_effect` are recorded as comparison arms only and are never an input to a sign table.

Draw voting:

- A `decide` call takes no vote: the returned distribution is the answer. A repeat of the same bytes is recorded under `repeat_index` and never voted.
- `generate` (design): the boundary takes N draws, records the vote and keeps the per-draw answers, because the instability is the model's.
- Measured on the predecessor: proposing which names are in play disagreed from draw to draw; typing the relation between two named companies did not. So the two steps are different calls, metered separately. The two figures are not quoted: their construction sits in the predecessor's archive (memo D-4).

The store (`~/.bellwether/modelgate`, or `BELLWETHER_MODELGATE`; never the vault):

| table | one row per | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `question_docs` | `question_version` | name and the file's sha256; the file itself is a blob |
| `floors` | (`question_version`, `model`) | the `seq` above which this pair labels, fixed by its first run |
| `run_events` | (`run_id`, event) | `started` (snapshot, caps and price in force), `ended`, `cost_estimate_broken`, `cost_model_acked` |
| `requests` | `idempotency_key` | digests, byte counts, `state_truncated`; no story field |
| `labels` | (`story_id`, `idempotency_key`) | the story's first-sighted row: `item_id`, `seq`, `observed_at` |
| `prior_coverage` | (`story_id`, `coverage_version`) | "Prior coverage", below: the cut it was counted over, `tag_count`, the tags and the three window counts, each window with its count per tag; tags and windows are NULL when `tag_count` is 0, and a `CHECK` holds `tag_count` to the length of the tag list |
| `attempt_events` | (`attempt_id`, event) | `opened` (worst-case cost), `answered` (status or transport failure kind, response sha256, both instants), `finalised` (outcome, cost, answering id), `abandoned` |

- Every table refuses `UPDATE` and `DELETE` by trigger; `PRAGMA synchronous=FULL`; one writer under a `LOCK` file.
- Order of writes for one call: `prior_coverage`, `requests` and the request blob, `labels`, `opened`, permit, send, response blob, then `answered` and `finalised` in one transaction.
- `user_version` is 2 since `prior_coverage` (2026-11-23). A store of version 1 is refused with `input_schema_mismatch`; none holds a row, because no run has written one (`store::tests::another_schema_version_an_unknown_request_and_a_write_through_the_dry_door_are_refused` holds the literal 2 and refuses a store of 1).
- `Store::write_answered` takes a `StoredBlob`, which only `Store::put_blob` returns, so the row cannot be written before the blob it names.
- No `answers` table and no `shadow stats` command: both are derivable from the blobs at any time.

The cost cap:

- Three required arguments, no defaults: `--run-cap-usd`, `--day-cap-usd` (the UTC day of `opened`), `--total-cap-usd` (the store's lifetime). Day and total are over the WHOLE store: every build, document and repeat index together.
- Before every send: `spent + worst_case(next) > cap` in any scope refuses it. No attempt row is opened and the run stops with `cost_cap_reached`.
- `worst_case` = request bytes × `--input-price-per-mtok` ÷ 1,000,000, rounded up. It is a bound only if one input token is at least one byte and each byte is billed once. Neither is verified for this vendor.
- `spent` = the vendor's cost where an attempt closed with one, else that attempt's worst case: an open, an abandoned and a cost-less closed attempt each count as spent.
- A stated cost of 0 is cost-less: measured 2026-11-23 on e304dcc, a stub stating `usage.cost: 0.0` took 3 sends through a run cap of 20 micro-USD against a worst case of 16 each. `requests.costless` counts answered attempts with no cost, per run.
- `--input-price-per-mtok 0` is `invalid_argument`: measured 2026-11-23 on e304dcc, a dry run with three caps of 0 and a price of 0 planned 2 requests and refused none.
- A vendor cost above its attempt's worst case writes `cost_estimate_broken` and stops the run. Every later run stops before its first send until one is started with `--ack-cost-model <run_id>`.
- `--ack-cost-model` naming a run with no `cost_estimate_broken` row is `invalid_argument` and writes nothing; naming one already acknowledged writes no second row.
- No warning mode.

The key:

- `BELLWETHER_MODEL_KEY_FILE` names a file holding it; one trailing newline is removed. No variable holds the value: a process environment is readable through `/proc` and `docker inspect`.
- `--dry-run` neither needs nor reads the key file: the binary hands it an exchange with no key and no socket.
- Refused before any row or socket: variable unset or file empty (`credential_key_missing`), file absent (`input_absent`), unreadable or not UTF-8 (`io_failed`), a control character or a space inside (`input_unparseable`), readable by group or others (`credential_key_exposed`).
- `ApiKey` has no `Display`, `Serialize` or `Clone`, and its `Debug` prints `ApiKey(<redacted>)`. One function reads the value, to build the `Authorization` header.
- The endpoint is a constant, redirects are off, and a transport failure is stored as a kind name, never as the client's own text.

#### ripple/2: what is asked, and of which model (2026-11-23)

- The owner's direction, 2026-11-23: look for new effects through model analysis of news; recognise negative and issuer-level events too; use a decision model wherever a judgment has a fixed answer space.
- ripple/2 = for each press release, an issuer layer (what happened to the company it is about) and a category layer (whether the event bears on a whole category of other companies, and how).
- **Stated tension:** a decision model is close to deterministic. It is the measuring instrument. The non-deterministic part of the direction, a generative model proposing affected company profiles, arrives with candidate retrieval and is not built.
- **Where a new effect can be:** issuer-level reactions to bad news are documented signals. The issuer layer is an instrument check. The hypothesis is the category layer.

| judgment | model | primitive | in `ripple-shadow/1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| source role | decision | choice | `source_role` |
| kind of content | decision | choice + noul | `content_kind`, `states_concrete_fact` |
| scope | decision | choice + noul | `scope`, `names_a_category_of_companies` |
| issuer event class, 36 classes, 21 of them adverse | decision | choice + noul | `event_class`, `any_listed_event_fits` |
| co-occurring adverse events (a release bundles results, a guidance cut and a departure) | decision | one noul per adverse class | 21 × `ev_<class>` |
| key-person circumstances | decision | noul × 9 | `kp_*`: departure, appointment, chief executive or founder, chief financial officer, long tenure, successor named, immediate, benign reason, linked to an investigation |
| issuer direction (comparison arm only) | decision | choice | `issuer_effect` |
| significance for the issuer, 4 ordered levels | decision | choice | `issuer_significance`: `none`, `minor`, `major`, `critical`, and `cannot_tell` off the scale |
| circumstances, asked whatever the class | decision | noul × 9 | `cx_*`: a state body acts against the company or its officers, criminal or national-security allegations against them, the act was required by another party, state bodies of more than one country act, a magnitude is stated, announced before this text, an interim successor, the company or its board states an investigation, the company calls the event material to its results or financial condition |
| a stated magnitude, in words | decision | choice | `cx_magnitude_size`: `not_stated`, `no_base` (a size and nothing to set it against), `small` (under about a tenth of what it is a part of), `large` (about a tenth or more) |
| stance toward a category, 6 stances + neutral + cannot tell | decision | choice, and 5 atomic nouls beside it | `stance_to_category`, `st_*` |
| significance for a category of other companies, the same 4 levels | decision | choice | `category_significance`: `none`, `minor`, `major`, `critical` |
| asymmetry between the issuer and the category | decision | noul × 5 | `as_*`: it matters more to others, the text describes the issuer as large or a leader, the text describes the others as small, early-stage or specialised, the issuer opens or standardises what others need, the text names the category or its problem as the purpose |
| cause scope | decision | choice | `cause_scope` |
| channel to other companies, 5 channels + none of these + cannot tell | decision | choice | `spillover_channel` |
| direction for the other companies (comparison arm only) | decision | choice | `spillover_effect` |
| relation typing for an (event, candidate) pair | decision | choice + noul | not asked: nothing produces candidates |
| affected company profiles, supporting span | generative | text | not asked: `generate` is design |

- The document: `services/modelgate/questions/ripple-shadow-1.json`, 64 questions (12 choice, 52 noul), 22,399 encoded bytes (`QuestionDoc::wire().len()`, 2026-11-23).
- `question_version` `c5b01e01851c0731b64a5dd553823d345aa07d57c701e24717d6824ae7f170d9`; `the_committed_ripple_shadow_document_parses_and_has_the_version_the_design_names` reads this line, the size and the counts above and the count of examples below, so an edit to the file without an edit here is red.
- `ripple-shadow/0` (45 questions, 16,280 bytes) was never sent and its file is deleted.

| from version 0 to 1 | encoded bytes |
|---|---|
| the 45 questions of version 0, reworded: "the company the text is mainly about", "its subject" and "the subject company" are all "the company reported on", the `kp_*` lead-in is shorter, a noul whose two descriptions said only yes and no says `Yes.` and `No.` | 16,280 to 15,331 |
| 17 new questions: `issuer_significance`, `category_significance`, 5 `as_*`, 9 `cx_*` nouls, `cx_magnitude_size` | 5,459, with their separators |
| 2 new questions, same name and file, never sent: `spillover_channel` (1,050), `spillover_effect` (559) | 20,790 to 22,399 |

- The owner's point, 2026-11-23: an event's weight depends on its circumstances. A chief executive forced out under an international scandal is not a planned retirement; an outlook lowered by 2% is not one lowered by 40%. The class label carries neither.

| part of the weight | who answers | state |
|---|---|---|
| the company's weight: market capitalisation, rank, the size ratio between the issuer and the affected companies | code, with the price collector | not built |
| scale and circumstances the text states | the model: the two significance questions, `cx_*`, `as_*` | asked in `ripple-shadow/1` |
| surprise: what the archive already said about the company | code: "Prior coverage", below | built; the company only, the matter is not matched |

- **Significance is relative** (owner, 2026-11-23): a large platform company releasing open AI models for calibrating quantum processors is minor for the issuer and major for small quantum companies.
  - It is asked twice, `issuer_significance` and `category_significance`, on one scale, and never as one "materiality".
  - Version 0's `materiality` asked the kind of content. It is `content_kind` now, and its instruction says a release is a new event however ordinary for its maker.
  - `category_significance` tells the model to judge the other companies alone, whatever the event means for the company reported on. It names neither direction.

| level | wording, the same for the issuer ("it") and the category ("those companies") |
|---|---|
| `none` | no effect on its business, finances or standing; for a category: the text describes no such category, or no effect on one |
| `minor` | an ordinary effect, of a size it meets in its normal course |
| `major` | a large effect, beyond its normal course: its results, plans or standing change markedly |
| `critical` | its survival, its control or most of its business changes, for better or worse |
| `cannot_tell`, issuer only | the text reports on no one company, or does not say enough; a regulator's rule for an industry is not `none` |

- A level is a size of effect and names no kind of event. Rejected 2026-11-23, levels worded by class (`major` as "a large change to its results, leadership, financing or legal position", `critical` as "at stake"): a planned retirement and a forced exit both read `major`, any offering read `major` whatever its size, and a favourable event had no top level.
- A single company the text names is not a category: `category_significance` reads `none` for it. That case is `scope` `named_counterparties` with `as_matters_more_to_others`. A 4-level scale for a named counterparty is not asked (D20).
- **Nothing is gated on the issuer's significance.** Every question is asked of every selected story (`every_question_is_asked_of_every_story_and_prior_coverage_is_recorded_and_never_sent`). A later gate to candidate retrieval reads `category_significance`, never `issuer_significance`.
- `as_issuer_described_as_large` and `as_others_small_or_specialised` record what the text says of size, apart: most releases call their issuer "leading" in a closing paragraph, so the first is expected near constant and one joint question would hide the second. The size ratio itself is data for code and is not asked.
- One phrase names the company in every question that needs it: "the company reported on". A law-firm alert reports on its target, not on the firm.
- Each new question asks what the text says ("According to the text", "Does the text say"), not what is true of the company: a build knows a real name's size and history.

| `cx_*` | yes only when | no also covers |
|---|---|---|
| `cx_state_body_acts_against` | a government, regulator, prosecutor, intelligence service or court acts against, investigates or charges the company or its officers | a state body that only approves, funds, buys or hears a private claim |
| `cx_criminal_or_security_allegation` | the allegations are against the company or its officers | civil claims only; the company as the victim |
| `cx_forced_by_another_party` | the text says a board, regulator, court, lender or exchange required the act | an act by choice, a commercial setback, a text that does not say |
| `cx_international_reach` | governments, regulators, prosecutors or courts of more than one country act in the matter | a company that sells or operates in several countries |
| `cx_previously_announced` | the event was announced before this text, or completes a plan announced before it | a scheduled notice, a forecast |
| `cx_investigation_open` | the company or its board states the investigation | another publisher of the text, such as a law firm, announcing its own |
| `cx_issuer_calls_it_material` | the company calls the event material to its results or financial condition | "not material", praise such as "a significant milestone", silence |

- `cx_magnitude_size` is a ratio alone. Rejected 2026-11-23, "or the text calls it material" inside `small` and `large`: "5% of its workforce in a substantial restructuring" fitted both, and `cx_issuer_calls_it_material` already asks for the word.
- `no_base` is the answer for an amount with nothing to set it against, such as an offering stated in dollars alone; `not_stated` contradicts `cx_magnitude_stated` true, and the other three contradict it false (K7).
- The boundary, a tenth of what the event is a part of, was written 2026-11-23 before any answer and is fitted to nothing. It is one boundary for every base: a 9% cut of a full-year outlook reads `small` (D20).
- `kp_successor_named` stays beside `cx_interim_successor_named`: both true is a contradiction (K7). `kp_linked_to_investigation_or_dispute` and `cx_investigation_open` ask different things, and no combination of the two contradicts.
- Examples: `services/modelgate/tests/fixtures/ripple-shadow-1.examples.json`, 20 synthetic stories, each with the options its author expects, and each with one expected `spillover_channel`. Hand-written; no model has read them; comparing a build's answers with them is not built.

| example | what it is there for |
|---|---|
| open models for calibrating quantum processors, twice: once stating the asymmetry outright, once in the words of a release | the owner's case: issuer `none` or `minor`, category `major` or `critical`, `whole_category`, `validates` or `lowers_cost_or_barrier` |
| the same company will build its own quantum processors | a threat to the category: `threatens_to_absorb`, category `major` or `critical` |
| an investment in one named small company | not a category: `named_counterparties`, `category_significance` `none`, `as_matters_more_to_others` |
| a founder forced out under charges in two countries; a planned retirement | one class, opposite circumstances and levels |
| an outlook lowered by 2%; by 40% | `small` against `large` |
| an offering of a stated amount | `no_base`; a regulator that only registers |
| a law-firm alert | the firm's investigation is not the company's |
| a central bank's rule for an industry | issuer `cannot_tell` |
| a handset maker lowers its forecast and its component orders; a power producer signs a 20-year contract for data centres that will use more than their owner buys today | `demand_falls` with `adverse`; `demand_rises` with `favourable` |
| a bank loses a quarter of its deposits and sells bonds at a loss; the text says nothing of other banks | `contagion`, `adverse` |
| a chip maker delays its next product for a defect of its own and lowers its forecast | `rival_weakened`, `favourable`: the list order decides against `demand_falls` |
| a trade ministry bars sales to one company | `state_action`, `adverse` |
| a contract won in a tender; a regulator declines an approval; the law-firm alert, the industry rule, the offering, both departures and the investment above | `none_of_these`: a court that hears a private claim, a rule for an industry, a refused approval and a charge against an officer alone are not `state_action`; a contract that states no change in what the buyer buys is not a demand option |
| the outlook lowered by 2%; by 40% | `demand_falls`: an outlook change of any size is a demand option; the 2% one expects `adverse` or `neutral` |
| a platform says a category's processors are ready, supports three makers and will sell its own | `none_of_these`, `spillover_effect` `mixed`, stance `validates` or `threatens_to_absorb` |
| a share repurchase; the open models and the platform entry above | `none_of_these`: no channel, or the stance carries it |

- The repository is public, so the answer spaces and the hypothesis are public (owner decision D15, open).
- All 64 questions are asked of every story in one request. Unverified: the predecessor's client states the vendor judges each question independently against the same state.
- The 15 classes that are not adverse have no `ev_` noul: with a noul for all but `routine_or_promotional` the encoded document measured 19,792 bytes (Python `json.dumps`, compact, 2026-11-23), above the 16,500-byte bound of that day.
- `undermines_category` is a stance: neither "absorbs" nor "substitutes" describes a statement that a category is years from usefulness.
- No question names the subject company: a decision model returns no text. Issuer resolution is code over the stored body, not built, so the issuer layer is not an alert.
- **Coverage, carried into any later claim:** the wires carry no NVIDIA product releases (16 hits for the name since 2026-11-19 are law-firm alerts; production store, read 2026-11-23). A chief executive's departure at a large company reaches this archive only through a wire release or an 8-K. The shadow would not have seen either of the owner's own examples.

#### The channel to other companies (`spillover_channel`, `spillover_effect`, 2026-11-23)

- Owner decision, 2026-11-23: ask through which channel an event reaches OTHER companies. The owner's review of 28 historical cases (27 under 10 relation labels and one expected spillover that did not occur; read that day, not committed) found four relations the stance list lacks.
- Form: a separate choice beside `stance_to_category`. Its options say what the text reports of the company reported on, never what follows for others; the group reached and its sign are the second table, read by code. The direction for the others is a second choice, a comparison arm.

| rejected form | symptom |
|---|---|
| the channels as further options of `stance_to_category` | not exclusive: a cloud company's long power contract both `validates` what power producers sell and raises demand, and the case review labels it with both. A demand signal needs two options for its two signs, so the list grows from 8 to 13 |
| one `demand_signal` option, its sign read from `spillover_effect` | the sign of an effect is then asked of the model, which this section forbids; rising or falling demand is a statement of the text |
| `contagion` and `rival_weakened` derived in code from `cause_scope` × an adverse class (this document until 2026-11-23) | `cause_scope` has no option for a customer's orders or a state body's act |
| options that end in the effect on others: "so its competitors can take its business", "may sit in similar companies too", "which also hurts its suppliers" (8ea32d3, 2026-11-23) | the clause is the hypothesis. Read as a condition, the model predicts the world; ignored, every own trouble reads `rival_weakened`. A failing bank or a late chip maker does not write the clause in its own release. "Hurts" and "more demand" inside the channel also built agreement with `spillover_effect` in |
| demand options reaching "suppliers and other sellers of the same thing" (8ea32d3) | one sign for two groups: a contract won in a tender is favourable for the winner's suppliers and adverse for the losing bidders |
| the tie-break "`state_action` first, then a demand option" (8ea32d3) | a delayed product with a lowered forecast read `demand_falls`, adverse, where the owner's third relation is favourable for rivals; `contagion` against `rival_weakened` had no order; it named option ids, which no other of the 64 instructions does |
| demand options without "expects to sell less" and "expects to sell more" | the owner's own case of the first relation, a phone maker lowering its forecast with no word on its orders, reads `none_of_these` (D20) |
| `contagion` worded as "the text ties the trouble to something similar companies share" | a bank's own release on a run names no other bank, so the option answers no real text of the owner's second relation |

| `spillover_channel`, in the document's order | the text reports, of the company reported on | others it reaches | sign for them |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state_action` | a government, a regulator, a prosecutor or a court restricts, penalises or charges it; not a charge against an officer alone, a private claim a court hears, a refused approval, or a rule for a whole industry | its suppliers, its customers, similar companies | adverse |
| `rival_weakened` | a delay, a defect, a recall or an outage of what it sells, from a cause inside it | its competitors | favourable |
| `demand_falls` | it, or a buyer of what it sells, will order, buy or spend less than before, or it expects to sell less | the suppliers of whichever company buys less | adverse |
| `demand_rises` | it, or a buyer of what it sells, will order, buy or spend more than before, or it expects to sell more | the suppliers of whichever company buys more, and other providers of what a buyer needs more of | favourable |
| `contagion` | it loses funding or deposits, takes losses on what it holds, or may be unable to pay what it owes | similar companies | adverse |
| `none_of_these` | none of the five | | none |
| `cannot_tell` | a text not clear enough to tell | | none |

- The sign column is the table code reads; written 2026-11-23 before any answer or return, fitted to nothing. It lives in this table and in `question::tests::CHANNEL_SIGNS`, and `each_channel_to_other_companies_fixes_their_sign_or_has_none` holds each row's last cell to the constant. No production code reads it yet.
- The order of the list is the tie-break: the instruction says "Where several fit, choose the one listed first." Written 2026-11-23, fitted to nothing. A delayed product with a lowered forecast reads `rival_weakened`; a regulator's order against a bank that lost its deposits reads `state_action`, adverse as `contagion` is.
- `contagion` and `rival_weakened` are two kinds of trouble the text states: in what the company holds or owes, or in what it sells. Whether similar companies share the first, or a rival can take the business of the second, is the hypothesis and is not asked.
- `rival_weakened` asks for a cause inside the company, as `cause_scope` `issuer_specific` does: `rival_weakened` with `industry_wide` is a K7 contradiction. `contagion` with `issuer_specific` is valid (a run on one bank) and is counted, because the adverse sign for similar companies is weakest there.
- A regulator's refusal of an approval reads `none_of_these`: the body does not act against the company, and the cause is not inside it.
- `none_of_these` is a statement about the text. Whether others are reached another way or not at all is read from `spillover_effect` and the stance.
- `spillover_effect` (`favourable`, `adverse`, `mixed`, `neutral`, `cannot_tell`) is a comparison arm, as `issuer_effect` is. `mixed` is for a text that states a gain for some companies and a loss for others; `cannot_tell` only where others are affected and the direction is not stated, so a text with no effect reads `neutral`. Its disagreement with the channel's sign is a K7 count.
- Only `spillover_effect` says "companies other than the company reported on", not "a category", so a single rival is reached too. The channel asks about the company reported on.
- A stance and a channel are answered apart. The six stances read `none_of_these` unless a channel also fits.
- Not asked, out of scope: a company moved because its name resembles another's (2 cases of the review), and index or investor decisions (3 cases). Neither is a relation the text of the event states.

| unguarded | what the table then says |
|---|---|
| an event that reaches two groups with opposite signs | one channel: a delayed product reads `rival_weakened`, favourable, though the maker's suppliers lose |
| a customer that leaves one seller for another | `demand_falls`, adverse for the seller's suppliers; nothing for the seller's rivals, who gain |
| a contract won in a tender | expected `none_of_these`; a build that reads `demand_rises` signs the losing bidders favourable |
| an outlook change of any size | a demand option: size is `cx_magnitude_size`, and K16 is split by `event_class` |
| a going-concern doubt at one small company | `contagion`, adverse for similar companies |
| a state act against one company | adverse, although a rival outside the act may gain; `spillover_effect` `favourable` beside it counts that case |
| a refused approval | `none_of_these`, although the maker of a competing product may gain |
| a rule for a whole industry | `none_of_these`: the owner's fourth relation is an act against one company |

#### Prior coverage (`modelgate::coverage`, built 2026-11-23; not run on production)

- Per selected story whose request was built, labelled or not: how many other stories of the same cut first carried one of its ticker tags earlier. Code computes it; no request carries it.
- Written before the send (`cmd_shadow::Run::cover`), from the row's whole `body`, not the cut state. A story the cap then refuses, or whose call fails, has a record: `prior_coverage.stories` counts records and can exceed `stories.labelled`.
- Earlier story: another `story_id` whose FIRST row carrying the tag in the SAME cut has an `observed_at` strictly before the story's first `observed_at` and at or after the window's start. Windows: 1, 7 and 30 days.
- A later row of an old story does not make it recent. Measured 2026-11-23 on 975ce19, which read every row: a story first held 26 days earlier and repeated 2 hours earlier counted 1 in the 1-day window.
- Count: per tag (`by_tag`), and pooled over the story's tags as distinct stories. A text naming a partner pools the partner's coverage with its own; `by_tag` keeps them apart, and which tag is the issuer is not known.
- `complete` is false when the cut's earliest `observed_at`, of any row, tagged or not, is after the window's start; the count is then a floor. The archive starts 2026-11-19, so every 30-day count is a floor until 2026-12-19.
- A story with no tag is stored as `tag_count` 0 with NULL counts, never as three zeros; a `CHECK` on the table refuses the mixed forms and a `tag_count` that is not the length of the tag list.
- One row per (`story_id`, `coverage_version`), and the first written stays: a later cut that holds a late-visible earlier row does not rewrite it. `snapshot_id` names the cut counted over.
- A new `coverage_version` is written only for stories selected after the change: a story already answered is not selected again, so it keeps its row under the old token alone. A recount is not built.
- `coverage_version`: `prior-coverage/1(ticker-tag/1;exchanges=NASDAQ,NASDAQGS,NASDAQGM,NASDAQCM,NYSE,NYSEAMERICAN,NYSEMKT,AMEX,NYSEARCA,OTC,OTCQB,OTCQX,OTCPINK,OTCMKTS,OTCMARKETS,OTHEROTC;ticker=1-5;class=1-2;days=1,7,30)`, built from the exchange list, the ticker and class lengths and the windows, so a change of any is another token and never pools with these rows. The parenthesis rule, the separators and the first-word rule are named `ticker-tag/1` by hand.

| `ticker-tag/1` | rule |
|---|---|
| group | the text between a `(` and the next `)`, holding no `(`, of any length |
| piece | the group split at `;` and `,` |
| pair | a piece with a `:`: the exchange before the first `:`, the ticker the first word after it |
| bare ticker | a piece with no `:` that is one ticker, read only while the last pair before it named an accepted exchange: `(NASDAQ: GGL, GGLA)` |
| exchange | upper-cased, spaces and `-` removed, then one of the 16 spellings in the token. A filter only: it is not part of the tag |
| ticker | 1 to 5 upper-case ASCII letters, then optionally `.` or `-` and 1 or 2 more; case is not folded |
| tag | the ticker, a class share written with `.`: `LRGP`, `HLD.B` |

- The tag is the ticker alone. Rejected 2026-11-23, `FAMILY:TICKER`: on 975ce19 an alert written `(NYSE: SMQ)` and the company's own `(NASDAQ: SMQ)` were two tags and the release read 0 earlier stories; a US ticker is one company across these venues at one time.
- `NYSE-MKT`, `OTC Markets` and `Other OTC` are spellings of the feeds' own ticker fields (`providers/open-web-feed/tests/fixtures/prn/sitemap_p1_1200.xml`, `gnw/rssfeed_0936_3_items.xml`); on 975ce19 each read as no tag.
- No length limit on a group: on 975ce19 a group of 12 pairs, 132 bytes, read as no tag under a limit of 120.

| not seen, or seen wrongly | effect |
|---|---|
| a release with no tag, a tag outside parentheses or in brackets | `no_tag` |
| a listing on an exchange outside the list: TSX, LSE, every other non-US venue | `no_tag`, or the US listing alone |
| an exchange written out (`Nasdaq Global Select Market`), two venues joined before one colon (`NASDAQ & TSX: ABC`), a foreign venue first in one piece (`TSX: ABC and NASDAQ: ABC`), a full-width colon | `no_tag` |
| a fund or an index in the same form: `(NASDAQ: QQQ)` | read as a company |
| a capitalised word after an accepted exchange: `(NYSE: A new listing)` | read as the ticker `A` |
| two share classes of one company | two tags, counted apart; `tag_count` 2 for one company |
| a company named without a ticker, which is most third-party text about a large company | not counted as an earlier story |
| a ticker passed to another company within 30 days | counted as one company |
| an earlier row with no body, or in no cut | not counted |
| the source of the earlier story | not read: a law-firm alert counts like a release. On a synthetic cut, 2026-11-23: 12 alerts in 4 days and no release by the company gave its first release 3, 12 and 12. For a large company the count is alert volume |
| a text naming several companies | the pooled count is every named company's coverage; `by_tag` has each, and nothing says which is the issuer |
| the matter | not matched: the count is about the company, not the event |
| visibility at the story's own instant | not asked: the order is `observed_at` within one cut, so a day-dated row observed earlier and visible only later counts when the cut holds it |

- Rejected, splitting the count by the earlier row's `source` or `provenance` column: `source` names the feed and `provenance` how the row was fetched, and a law-firm alert arrives on the same feed as a company's release. The split needs `source_role`, which only the model answers.
- The grammar is written from the wire convention and measured on no production body. The share of `no_tag` is unknown until the first dry run reports it. One bound from the feed side, not the body: 345 of 1,065 unique PRN sitemap urls carried a non-empty `news:stock_tickers` (§11.5).
- Reader: the envelope's `prior_coverage`: `version`, `stories`, `no_tag`, `tagged`, `several_tags`, and per window `none` (tagged stories with no earlier story), `some`, `none_for_a_tag` (stories with a tag that has none), `max` and `incomplete`. A run reads back the rows it wrote; a dry run reports the records it would write.

#### The shadow run (`modelgate shadow run`, built 2026-11-23; not run)

- Record only: no test, no list, no price. The command has no returns input, and `modelgate` depends on no crate of the news side (§8 row MG10).
- Input: one `newsvault cut` snapshot directory, validated by `snapshot_contract::validate` first. `items --at` has no body column; reading the vault's SQLite would be a second copy of the visibility rule.
- Unit: a story. One label per `story_id` per (question version, build, repeat index), on its first-sighted row: lowest `observed_at`, then lowest `seq`. A later row of the story is counted `repeat_of_story` and never sent.

| a first-sighted row is | counted as | sent |
|---|---|---|
| at or below the floor | `below_floor` | no |
| outside the 10% sample under `--sample-only` (first byte of sha256(`story_id` ‖ `ripple-shadow-sample-1`) below 26) | `outside_sample` | no |
| without a body | `no_body` | no |
| observed on or before the build's date (`ModelId::predates`) | `build_postdates_story` | no |
| linked to a request answered `ok` | `already_labelled` | no |
| linked to a request answered `empty` or `unparseable`, and to none answered `ok` | `already_unusable` | no |
| linked to a request with at least one attempt and no answer, and observed more than `--give-up-after-hours` ago | `gave_up` | no |
| linked to no answered request, body identical to an answered one | `already_answered`, a `labels` row, and `labelled` or `unusable` by that answer | no |
| anything else | `selected` | yes |

- **Selection is an anti-join, not a cursor.** A day-dated row enters a later cut with a `seq` below rows already labelled (§3.0, "Selection"); a `seq` cursor would skip it for ever (`a_row_that_becomes_visible_late_is_still_labelled`).
- The floor is fixed by the first run of a (question version, build): `--from-seq`, else the cut's `seq_high_water`, so nothing already collected is labelled by default. A later run naming another floor is `invalid_argument`.
- **A build never labels a story it could have read**: the build's date must be before the UTC day of `observed_at`. The date is the id's suffix, an inference, not a vendor statement of a knowledge cutoff.
- A build dated before a story can label it later with no leak while that build is served. What cannot be recovered: the answers of a build after it is retired, the answers of a build re-served under the same id, and the label lag.
- Retry: a transport failure and 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529; at most 3 attempts per request per run, each its own attempt row; wait 2 s × the attempt, or `Retry-After`, capped at 30 s. Any other status is final for the run.
- A failed story is asked again by later runs until it is older than `--give-up-after-hours`. Three stories failing in a row stop the run (`vendor_failing`).
- A story linked and never attempted (the cap refused it, or the process died between `labels` and `opened`) is selected again whatever its age: its age counts failed attempts, and it has none.
- A never-visible (`Undated`) row is in no cut and is never labelled; `no_body`, `build_postdates_story` and `gave_up` are the envelope's counts of what else was not.

| exit | when | stdout |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | no attempt of this run failed or closed `empty` or `unparseable`, or nothing was new, or a dry run, or `--limit` stopped it | `modelgate.shadow_run/1` |
| 8 | `store_failed` (a store failure after a paid send; its text under `store.failure`), `cost_estimate_broken`, `cost_cap_reached`, `partial_shadow` (a story failed and another was answered, or a failure was not transient), `unusable_answer` (an attempt of this run closed `empty` or `unparseable`); `exit.error_code` names the first that applies, in this order | the envelope |
| 7 | `vendor_unreachable` (nothing answered, every failure transient), `lease_held` | empty; `modelgate.error/1` on stderr, the envelope under `details` |
| 4 | `input_absent`: the snapshot, the question file, the key file | empty |
| 2 | `invalid_argument`, `input_unparseable`, `input_schema_mismatch`, `credential_key_missing`, `credential_key_exposed`, `io_failed` | empty |

- `--dry-run` validates, selects, builds every request and applies the caps; it opens the store read-only, takes no lease, reads no key, and writes and sends nothing. `planned_estimate` is null until 100 costed attempts of the same version and build exist.
- The envelope reads the store back: outcomes, `requests.costless`, the three spends, label lag (p50, p90, max of `received − observed_at`), the answering ids, `questions.answered` / `not_answered` / `missing` parsed from this run's `ok` response blobs, and `prior_coverage` ("Prior coverage").
- `stories.labelled` counts `ok` answers only; `stories.unusable` counts the `empty` and `unparseable` ones.

What the shadow measures. A number is read per `question_version` and never across two; a threshold marked "owner" is written here before the first paid call (D10), with the least number of sessions a version must have before it is read.

| # | measurement | how | kills or changes the plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | frequency of category events | stories per week: `source_role` `issuer_own`, `content_kind` `new_fact`, `scope` `whole_category`, stance not `neutral` or `cannot_tell` | owner: not set |
| K2 | frequency of adverse issuer events | stories per week with an adverse class, `issuer_own`, per class | owner: not set |
| K3 | repeat noise | `--repeat-index 1` and `2` on the sample: top-option flip rate, mean absolute probability difference | owner: not set |
| K4 | determinism | share of byte-identical responses to byte-identical requests, with the gap between the sends: a repeat seconds later may be a cache hit | none; decides whether repeats continue |
| K5 | order sensitivity | a second document with another option order, on the sample | owner: not set |
| K6 | wording sensitivity | a reworded document on the sample | owner: not set |
| K7 | self-consistency | `stance_to_category` against the `st_*` nouls; `event_class` against `ev_*` and `any_listed_event_fits`; `category_significance` above `none` with `names_a_category_of_companies` false; `cx_magnitude_stated` true with `cx_magnitude_size` `not_stated`, or false with any other size; `kp_successor_named` and `cx_interim_successor_named` both true; a signed `spillover_channel` against `spillover_effect`, counted apart for the opposite sign, `neutral` and `mixed` ("The channel to other companies"); `state_action` with `cx_state_body_acts_against` false; `rival_weakened` with `cause_scope` `industry_wide`. Not a check: a signed channel with `scope` `issuer_only` (in the case review the companies reached were mostly absent from the text); `contagion` with `cause_scope` `issuer_specific`; `kp_linked_to_investigation_or_dispute` with `cx_investigation_open`, where all four combinations are valid (the link may be a dispute; an investigation may concern no person) | owner: not set |
| K8 | class list fit | share of `issuer_own` + `new_fact` stories whose `any_listed_event_fits` is below one half | none; a high share revises the list (a new version) |
| K9 | noise share | share of `third_party_solicitation` and `not_a_company_event` | none; sizes the gate |
| K10 | time | label lag p50, p90 | owner: not set |
| K11 | cost | vendor cost per story against the estimate | owner: the yearly budget |

Not verified, because it needs a paid call or the VPS; the write path stores raw bytes so none of these can lose a label:

- the response shape (`answers`, `usage.cost`, `model`), taken from the predecessor's client. If the answers sit under another key, every call closes `empty` (final) and each run exits 8 `unusable_answer`;
- how the vendor reports an error inside a 2xx: only a top-level `error` member beside no answer is read as `failed`;
- the refusal shape; a refused question is counted `not_answered` whatever it looks like;
- the question wire shape (`type`, `instructions`, `criteria`), and whether the vendor keeps the order of a JSON object's keys;
- whether a build is shown a choice's options together and in the document's order: the tie-break of `spillover_channel` is that order;
- whether a dated request echoes its dated id;
- billed tokens against request bytes, and whether the state is billed once or once per question;
- whether a byte-identical request returns identical bytes; the rate limit; how long a dated build is served;
- the size limit: the predecessor's one non-transport refusal in 23,823 calls was an HTTP 400 on a 180,725-character title against the vendor's 32,000-token limit (its `2026_10_jev_feature_layer.py`, read 2026-11-23). The 35,800-byte ceiling is above 32,000, so it is under that limit only if a token averages at least 1.12 bytes (35,800 ÷ 32,000); the largest request the committed document can produce is 35,563 bytes (36 + 128 + 13,000 + 22,399), which needs 1.11; 34,200 needed 1.07, and 30,000 held at one byte per token. An inference, not a measurement: the predecessor's 32,000-character states and their questions passed that limit. A full-length story refused here closes `failed` with a 400, final for the run, and shows in K12;
- body sizes in the production store, so the truncated share; the predecessor measured its harder question gaining about 6 AUC points up to a 32,000-character cap, above this budget of 13,000 bytes;
- the size and duration of a production `newsvault cut` beyond §3.0's first real one (4,333 items, 1.05 s, 2026-11-22); distinct stories per day.

Not built, and why it can wait:

| item | why |
|---|---|
| reading answers out of the blobs (`shadow stats`, an `answers` table) | derivable at any time; a table would freeze a parser written from an unverified shape |
| repeats, another option order, a reworded document | need only the same build still served: `--repeat-index`, `--sample-only`, a second `--questions` file |
| a second build in parallel | a second timer line; lost only if that build is retired before it starts |
| a daily fixed synthetic request compared across days | would detect a build re-served under its id; until then that is unguarded |
| `generate`, `score`, spans, candidate retrieval, relation typing, the sign tables, returns | no producer |
| company weight (market capitalisation, rank) and the size ratio between an issuer and the affected companies | data for code; arrives with the price collector |
| a gate from the shadow's answers to candidate retrieval | no retrieval exists; when built it reads `category_significance` |
| prior coverage by matter, by source role, or for a company with no tag | needs the answers read out of the blobs, and issuer resolution |
| a recount of prior coverage under a new `coverage_version` for stories already answered | pure code over a cut; nothing reads the counts yet |
| prior coverage keyed on the feeds' own ticker fields (`news:stock_tickers`, the GNW stock category) | a cleaner key than the body; `SnapshotRow` does not carry them |
| company newsrooms, 8-K items, spoken statements | new sources with their own robots and budget decisions |
