## 10. What this document leaves open

- Nothing of the shape is open; what is open is a choice taken by default, an assumption no measurement places, an unmeasured cost or a provisional number, with owner decisions and built comparators beside them.
- N1 and N2 are recorded below; beyond this section the memo's own list stays open.
- Decision ids: `D1`, `D3`, `D5` are this document's, set out below; `S7-D1` to `S7-D11` are the owner's step-7 decisions of 2026-11-17 (§11.2, §11.5 step 7); `PG-D1` to `PG-D9` are the owner's decisions of 2026-11-17 after the PRN/GNW research ("tak, zgadzam sie z rekomendacjami"); `D-1` to `D-8` are the memo's §8 table and are written `memo D-n` here.
- Memo D-1 (which vendor for history): closed 2026-11-22 as "no purchases" (owner: no paid sources); memo §10 step 5's backfill to 246 sessions has no vendor.
- The 12-month history can come only from free paths, such as the wires' own sitemaps; unmeasured: how far back the PRN, GNW and Business Wire sitemaps go.
- A free archive read now has an observation time equal to the fetch, weeks after publication, so it gives no historical cutoff before its own fetch.
- Two coverage reads of the news store join without an index: `store::covered_story_ids` and `store::coverage_up_to`. Measured 2026-11-24 on a laptop with Python `sqlite3` 3.53.4 over a synthetic store holding the join columns only (876,009 attempts and 797,694 items: 365 days at 2,347 attempts and 2,134 items a day, plus 19,354 attempts and 18,784 items of the filings layout §9 rejects): `covered_story_ids` for one window took 2.9 s, and 0.00013 s with indexes on `attempts(source, target_window)` and `items(attempt_id)`. `coverage_up_to` over 570 windows of the same store was not run to its end without them (one run stopped at 120 s, the same day) and took 0.07 s with them. Not re-measured on news rows alone (97.8% of those attempts) or on the VPS. Open: a `newsvault` fix on its own branch, two indexes in one schema step with a test asserting both query plans.
- How PRN and GNW are read so that no stretch between polls goes uncovered: decided 2026-11-17 by the owner; the plan is §11.2's completeness table, whose PRN sitemap row and GNW row are built and PRN archive row is not. Their 20-item RSS indexes left uncovered stretches at both periods (§11.2's period table, measured 2026-11-16). Still open: when a PRN monthly archive is published and whether it is complete.
  - Decided 2026-11-17 ~21:30Z (owner, "tak"), option A: the GNW walk has no cap of its own; it is bounded by its id range and, once step 7 builds it, by S7-D3's deadline, and its ids are outside S7-D6's cap (§11.5 step 7): `walk_ids_are_never_counted_against_the_cap_or_deferred` (the queue) and `a_walked_poll_past_the_cap_sends_every_walk_id_and_defers_listed_releases_only` (through `collect`), 2026-11-18.
  - Decided the same day: a walked id answered 410 is never asked again, under its slug or another; asking 410 ids again is decided on live data (`ledger`'s `walk.gone`); S7-D5's carry does not ask one again, since a 410 is held and its row is closed `held` (§3.2's `deferred_closed`).
  - Also open: whether a GNW id stays non-public for long after a higher id is listed (an embargo); probe10 bounds it at 20.6%, not at zero (§11.6).
  - Also open: the PRN October 2026 archive was 2.27 MB gzipped (research 2026-11-17); its decoded size is unknown, so whether it fits open-web's `BODY_LIMIT` of 8 MiB (§11.1), which counts decoded bytes, is unknown; over it, it is a `PermanentFailure` stored cut. Whether its `<lastmod>` is the publication time was not checked.
- Memo D-1 does not block `edgar-press`'s `vendor_archive` backfill: it collected against live EDGAR on 2026-11-13 behind the probed lag (D5 below, §8 rows R11, R20).
- Any `vendor_archive` history needs its own probed lag, because a lag is keyed by (source, provenance); today only `edgar-press`'s `plan` asks for one (§8 row R11).

**Three decisions taken by default on 2026-11-13.**

- The owner was asked twice, chose neither, and said to build anyway: each is the design's own recommendation, an assumption, not a settled fact, reversed where its fork bullet names (two functions for D1, one constant for D3, three places for D5).
- **D1, what `1` means.** `1` is **the answer is no**: `newsvault ledger --check` exits 1 on a coverage shortfall and `panel-contract validate` keeps its verdict there; `input_unparseable`, `input_schema_mismatch` and `io_failed` exit `2` (§5.1).
  - Callers: `git grep -n newsvault -- '*.yml' '*.py' '*.sh'` on 2026-11-13 returned two hits, a comment in `ci.yml` and a docstring in `probes/parity_baseline.py`, neither runs the binary; the one caller in the tree now is `probes/newsvault_parity.py`, reading `newsvault day`'s `0` (a result it compares) and `2` (a day that reader refused), never `1`, which `day` cannot return. Callers outside the tree: unknowable.
  - **The other fork is three functions:** `exit_code` in `services/newsvault/src/main.rs` decides every FAILURE exit; `news_provider::Exit` decides every exit a successful `collect` takes, including the stdout rule; `cmd_robots::RobotsExit` decides a successful `robots refresh`'s, its 1 included, and defers to `news_provider::Exit` for 7 and 8; nothing else branches on an exit status.
- **D3, the partition key.** The **publication day**, `items/valid_date=<D>/`, because the label is then a true statement about the rows under it; a day-dated row goes under the day it names, not under an instant nothing published. Its cost is §5's own row.
  - Cost of not having it, measured: 9 of 287 items in the predecessor's `session_date=2026-07-01` partition were published outside that UTC day, 3.14%.
  - Not a seq range: it can be declared complete, but its day-query scan cost is unmeasured.
  - **The fork is one constant:** `VALID_DATE` in `services/newsvault/src/store.rs`, `substr(COALESCE(i.valid_at, i.valid_day, i.valid_minute, i.valid_refused), 1, 10)` since 2026-11-15, which `covered_by_a_segment()`, `Committer::unpublished_rows` and `cmd_items` build from; `publish::partition_of` is the only place it becomes a path.
    - A `minute` row goes under its UTC day, the calendar its value is stated in.
    - `cmd_items` held its own copy of the expression until 2026-11-15; it now reads the constant.

- **D5, a backfill with no probe behind it.** Refused, not dated: a `vendor_archive` window is refused before its first request unless a `MeasuredLag` with a probe id, a non-zero probe count and a positive lag a chrono `TimeDelta` holds stands behind it (§8 row R11).
  - **The lag that stands behind EDGAR, measured 2026-11-13:** `94,922 s = 26.37 h`, the MAX of 22 per-filing lags over the two days the vendor's quarter listing named; each lag is the instant the vendor states it last wrote `form.<day>.idx` minus that filing's `<ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME>`; the run spent 27 requests of a registered 30. Registration, run log and the four refusals the run did not reach: `probes/observation_lag/PREREGISTRATION.md`; per-filing numbers: `observation_lag_results.json` beside it.
  - It falls in the registered band `24 h - 7 d`, so **the backfill is permitted only with the session shift written into the panel and no day column may mix backfilled and live items** - every backfilled item's membership moves by more than one session.
  - The max, not the registered p90 (`57,561 s`, inside 24 h): chosen and exercised offline before the first request, and the reason for the harder band; the registration's amendment dated 2026-11-13 carries the arithmetic.
  - `leaks` counts sampled filings above the scalar, so under a max `leak_rate()` is `0.0` by construction and says nothing about the vendor; the informative count is index rows whose `Date Filed` is not their own index's day, **0 of 384 and 0 of 549** on these two days.
  - **How the number reaches a run:**
    - `--lag-policy` names a hashed policy file holding one `MeasuredLag` per (source, provenance), keyed by both because one adapter read live and read earlier are two populations (R10); `news_provider::lag_policy::LagPolicy::read` is its only constructor; `cmd_collect::open_provider` hands the entry to `EdgarPress::with_observation_lag`; the committed policy is `news-provider/policy/observation-lag.json`.
    - The policy's bytes are archived before the plan (`cmd_collect::copy_policy_into_vault`, called from `cmd_collect::run`); the run envelope names policy, probe and lag (`cmd_collect::envelope_of`); not the item row: §3.1's `Item` has no observation-lag field (no column added: nothing would read it), so a stored item reaches the probe through its `attempt_id` and that run's envelope.
    - Measured 2026-11-13 against live EDGAR with the policy: window `2026-11-12`, run date `2026-11-13`, 1 index request planned, `vendor_archive` arm on all 5 attempts, 4 items committed from a 3-CIK roster out of 7,805 vendor rows, 5 requests spent; without `--lag-policy` it refuses at exit 2 with `no lag entry` before any request.
  - **Which instant a backfilled row carries: `valid + seconds`, with `valid` raised to the listing index day's start (an on-time instant row) or end (any other row), not the fetch clock (§3.1, §8 row R11).** Not the fetch clock: it RECORDS when we read, years late on a real backfill. `valid + seconds` is the COUNTERFACTUAL a point-in-time study wants, one number per source, loose by the spread of acceptance times inside a filing day; a date is bounded at the END of its own calendar day plus the lag.
    - That looseness, measured on the run above while rows were still dated by the fetch clock: the four items' `observed_at` `2026-11-13T17:44:5x Z` against `valid_at + 94,922 s` differ by **not one sign** - `-5.81 h`, `-5.82 h`, `+2.17 h`, `+2.16 h`; the two negatives are the max scalar loose for a row whose own lag was `5.85 h`.
  - **Two places decide it.** WHICH instant: `edgar-press`'s `EdgarPress::backfill_observation`, `Visibility::from_backfill`'s one production caller; it moves into `pit::datedness` beside `end_of_day` when a second `vendor_archive` provider exists, so two providers cannot date one `Published` value differently. By design, no code: `filingvault` is that second caller (§12.3; the move is §12.8 step 6). WHETHER a row may carry a placed instant: `cmd_collect`'s `Committer::rows_of` stores one for `vendor_archive`, refuses an archive row with none and a `live_ingest` row with one.
  - **The other fork is three places:** `news_provider::provider::probed_lag` holds the six conditions; `edgar-press`'s `plan` is the one caller that asks; `LagPolicy::read` decides what a policy file may say.
- **The provenance boundary, which D5 needs and no measurement places.** A window whose last day is on or before the run's own UTC date is a live ingest and an earlier one a vendor archive; an assumption, not a figure: how long an EDGAR daily index keeps growing is unmeasured, so there is no quantile to put here.
  - **The one place to change it** is `edgar-press`'s `Provider::provenance`, also home of the fail-closed arm: a window nothing can read takes the archive arm, the one that refuses.
- **The backfill coverage convergence, a vertical slice 2026-11-13 (§8 row R20).** Three choices, each changeable in one place.

| choice | rule | **the one place to change it** |
|---|---|---|
| **Which arm converges** | a `vendor_archive` follow-up whose story the store already holds a committed item for is dropped; `edgar-press` always issues a `live_ingest` one (R16); so a re-run fetches only the uncovered accessions. `open-web-feed` is live only and drops a follow-up whose story is held (§11.1) | `edgar-press`'s `EdgarPress::follow_ups_to_issue`; a second provider with a different vendor-row identity maps a follow-up to its story in its own `Provider::story_of` and nowhere else |
| **The denominator** | `MAX(matched)` over a window's index attempts, because each run's index records the same in-universe count and `SUM` would multiply it by the number of runs | `newsvault::store`'s `coverage_up_to` |
| **The gate** | `newsvault ledger --check` raises `coverage_incomplete` whenever `covered < planned`, on a gap of ANY size - no percentage, no tolerance, because a threshold chosen after seeing a result is forbidden here | the `coverage_incomplete` push in `cmd_ledger`'s `read` |

- **The transient-retry bound, taken by default 2026-11-13 (§8 rows R19, R21).** A document fetch that fails transiently (HTTP 503, or a transport error other than a body over the profile's `body_limit`) is re-attempted within the run, bounded by `MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES` = 2, a MECHANISM cap on the work spent per request whose only job is to stop one persistently failing accession stalling the run; what still fails is a coverage gap R20 converges or the next run fills.
  - Not a figure read off the ~8% transient loss measured that day: deriving a retry count from the observed rate is choosing a threshold after seeing the result.
  - **The one place to change it** is the `MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES` constant in `news_provider::collect` (re-exported from the crate root); the rate it is spaced at is R19's, not this knob's.
- **The per-host pace, taken by default 2026-11-14 (§8 row R19).** Three choices; the first two change in `news_provider`.
  - **The key** is the request url's host, lowercased, not the source and not the registrable domain, so two sources asking one host share a bucket and `sec.gov` beside `www.sec.gov` would not; changed in `Wire::wait_out_the_host` and `HostKey::new`, the file name in `BudgetScope::file_name`.
  - `HostKey::new` refuses a trailing dot since 2026-11-15, because `host.` and `host` are one host and would be two buckets and two hosts-file rows: `a_host_key_breaking_any_one_rule_is_refused` (mutation 2026-11-15, the check removed: red). No committed url or hosts row ends in a dot (grep 2026-11-15).
  - **The order** is host wait first, then the per-IP reservation, so a slow host never holds an IP slot other hosts queue behind; the per-IP wait then leaves a host slot late, and the send gate makes the call wait that out at its socket (§8 row R19, hole 6, closed 2026-11-22); changed in `Wire::send`.
  - **The SEC declaration**, 100 ms per host for `www.sec.gov`, the same interval as its per-IP pace, lives in `edgar-press`'s `transport()`; setting it to `None` returns the run to the per-IP pace alone.
- **Per-host queues, owner decision 1 of 2026-11-17** ("tak, zgadzam sie z rekomendacjami"; §8 row R19). Option (a): open-web's `RequestBudget::min_interval` is `None`, so its per-IP pace is gone and each admitted host is its own queue.
  - Unchanged: the `per_host` floor (7 s since 2026-11-19, the next bullet), the Crawl-delay refusal (owner decision 1, 2026-11-16), `Retry-After` holds and 5xx doubling, each per host as before.
  - Unchanged: edgar's 100 ms per-IP pace, because SEC counts its limit per IP.
  - Own queue means own slots, not concurrency: a host's next slot depends only on `pace/<host>.per-host`, its own hold and its own doubling. One process still sends one request at a time, so a wait on host A still delays, in wall time, every request behind it; host B's next request owes only B's own floor (`a_hold_on_one_host_leaves_another_host_owing_only_its_own_floor`). The stop deadline (§11.2) is per run.
  - The 50% busy bound (§11.1 Pace) is read per host; the run's wall time is set by the send order (next bullet).
  - PRN and CNW, owner decision of 2026-11-17 ("zgadzam sie z Twoja rekomendacja"): each keeps its own per-host queue; no per-vendor bucket. Both are Cision and cross-list releases (§11.5 step 6), so our combined rate to the two can be 2 requests per 7 s, against at most 1 under the shared queue. `dig +short` 2026-11-17: PRN (`www.prnewswire.com`) 104.18.36.40, 172.64.151.216; CNW (`www.newswire.ca`) 104.16.44.11, 104.16.45.11; no shared limit is known, and none is ruled out.
- **The per-host interval, 7 s, owner decision 1 of 2026-11-19** (§8 row R19). It amends owner decision 1 of 2026-11-16 (the Crawl-delay refusal) and of 2026-11-17 (per-host queues), both stated at 10 s. Two constants, held apart: `open_web_feed::INTERVAL` (the profile's `per_host`) and `cmd_collect::PACE_FLOOR` (the floor `collect` checks it against).
  - Basis, measured 2026-11-19 over all 11 production collect runs 09:36–17:14 UTC by two methods (SQL over the `deferred` tables; parsing the stored index payloads), which agreed within 3%:

    | host | largest interval needing no carry in any run | its binding run (UTC) | requests in the window | largest interval needing no carry in 90% of runs |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | PRN | 5.72 s | 14:30 | 152 in 864 s | 7.19 s |
    | GNW | 7.29 s | 15:00 | 120 in 868 s | 7.48 s |
    | Yahoo | 11.99 s | 15:00 | 73 in 863 s | 13.56 s |
    | Fed | never binding | — | — | — |

  - Construction: interval = W_host / (DEMAND − 1); W_host = the run's deadline − the host's first `requested_at`; DEMAND = index requests + fresh documents + walk ids + retries (fetched plus first-time deferred); the carried backlog excluded.
  - Politeness reference, the owner's judgement and not a measurement: Common Crawl news-crawl `fetcher.server.delay` 9.0 s (`commoncrawl/news-crawl`, `conf/crawler-conf.yaml`); Apache Nutch `fetcher.server.delay` 5.0 s (`nutch-default.xml`); trafilatura 5 s; Heritrix 3–30 s.
  - The single-thread round-robin does not bind at 7 s: the active hosts' median request times summed to 1.2–4.0 s in those runs; single requests reached 15.4 s (Yahoo) and 9.8 s (GNW).
  - Rule unchanged: a robots `*` Crawl-delay above `INTERVAL` refuses the host (`CrawlDelayOverInterval`, §10's robots rows).
  - One host asks at most ⌊870 s / 7 s⌋ + 1 = 125 requests in a 30-min run (§11.2's run-length bullets).
  - Rejected: 10 s (2026-11-16 to 2026-11-19): PRN needed 5.72–7.19 s at the US morning peak, so 10 s queued 60–160 PRN stories per run.
  - Tests: §8 row R19's robots floor and transport cells.
- **Round-robin by host, owner decision of 2026-11-17** ("zgadzam sie z Twoja rekomendacja", after owner decision 1; §8 rows R19, R21). `collect` keeps one lane per url host (`news_provider::collect::HostQueue`) and serves the lanes in turn, one request each, so one host's wait also runs down the other hosts' floors.
  - Unit: the url host by `budget::host_of`, the key `Wire` paces by; a url it cannot key goes to one extra lane, and `Wire` refuses or fails it as before.
  - Tie-break: lanes in the order their host first entered the queue; a turn starts at the lane after the last one served. The plan's order decides it, so the order, and every attempt's ordinal and `attempt_id`, is a function of the plan and the answers (`a_replayed_committed_hosts_run_gives_every_attempt_the_same_id_and_url`).
  - Follow-ups and retries go to the back of their own host's lane, so a follow-up still leaves after its index and a retry still waits its host's pace (§8 row R21); carried requests wait behind all of them (S7-D5, §11.5 step 7 PR 5).
  - One host is one lane (a lane per url instead: red, 8 tests, both `wire` tests of §8 row R19 among them, mutation 2026-11-17), so one host with nothing carried is a plain FIFO (`one_host_is_one_lane_and_keeps_the_fifo_order`). EDGAR's order (`www.sec.gov` only) is unchanged (`an_edgar_run_on_its_one_host_keeps_the_fifo_order_retries_last`, which checks the order only: one-request lanes served in turn give the same FIFO). `--dry-run` prints counts and no order, so its output is unchanged.
  - Still one request at a time: concurrency was not chosen; between SourceIds it stays §11.3's target.

    | send order, 10 s floor, no request time | round-robin by host | block order (before) | shared queue | construction |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | three loopback hosts, 3 indexes, 2 pages each, A's first page answered 408 and retried | 30 s | 40 s | 90 s | round-robin: `round_robin_by_host_overlaps_the_host_floors_through_a_real_wire`, `WaitedClock` waits summed, 2026-11-17; block order: the same test with one lane for every host (mutation 2026-11-17); shared: arithmetic, 9 waits of 10 s |
    | two loopback hosts, 8 requests | 30 s | 50 s | 70 s | probe test 2026-11-17, not kept (PR #38 review) |
    | two loopback hosts: A's index and 1 page answered 408 three times; B's index and 3 pages | 30 s | 40 s | not computed | probe test over `driven_through_a_wire` 2026-11-17, not kept; block order: one lane for every host |
    | two loopback hosts: A's index and 1 page answered 503 `Retry-After: 120`, then 200; B's index and 4 pages | 150 s | 130 s | not computed | round-robin: `a_hold_on_one_host_delays_the_other_hosts_turns_under_round_robin`, waits 0, 0, 10, 0, 120, 0, 10, 10 s, 2026-11-17; block order: the same test with one lane for every host, waits 0, 0, 10, 0, 10, 10, 10, 90 s (mutation 2026-11-17); B's last 3 pages leave about 120 s later |
    | refetch worst-case poll: 4 indexes + 20 GNW + 20 PRN + 100 CNW + 20 Fed follow-ups | 1,000 s | 1,570 s | 1,630 s | arithmetic 2026-11-17, not measured: round-robin is CNW's own 100 waits; block order is GNW's 20 waits, then PRN's 19, CNW's 99 and the Fed's 19; 36.3% shorter than block order (27.5% with three hosts, 1,000 s against 1,380 s) |

  - The run's busy time, summed over hosts, does not depend on the send order: the refetch worst case at 7 s is 4,340 + 4,340 + 21,700 + 4,340 (the Fed) = 34,720 s a day; its wall time is about the busiest host's waits, 31 × 700 s = 21,700 s, 25.12% of 86,400 s, unchanged by the Fed (arithmetic 2026-11-19, request times not counted).
  - Deferred by the owner until the first live data (2026-11-17 ~16:10Z, "zgoda" to the step-7 critique, §11.5 step 7), earliest-due-first: picks the host whose slot is due soonest, so it reads each host's pace file and the clock before every pick, a second reader of the pace beside `Wire::send`; of the table above, only the `Retry-After` row could be shorter under it. That is its one gain, not built: it would serve other hosts while one host is under a hold, which round-robin waits out on that host's turn (§8 row R19, hole 12).
  - Not built, open (owner): retries in a lane of their own, served after every first attempt. Measured 2026-11-17 by the mutation that does it inside `HostQueue`, on the table's rows: 30 s on the three-host row (as round-robin), 40 s on the 408-three-times row (as block order), 130 s on the `Retry-After` row (as block order). It would change §8 row R21's "back of its host's lane" and its tests.
  - Rejected, lanes sorted by host name: also deterministic, but the order would no longer follow the hosts file's order (§11.2: GNW, then PRN, CNW and the Fed).
  - Rejected, concurrent sends: not chosen by the owner (2026-11-17).
  - **The one place to change it** is `HostQueue` in `news-provider/src/collect.rs`; keying every request to one lane restores the block order, and turns `the_queue_serves_three_hosts_round_robin_in_the_order_each_host_first_appeared`, `a_retry_goes_to_the_back_of_its_host_lane_and_stops_at_the_cap`, `a_retry_on_a_short_lane_is_served_in_its_host_turn_while_a_longer_lane_drains`, `round_robin_by_host_overlaps_the_host_floors_through_a_real_wire`, `a_hold_on_one_host_delays_the_other_hosts_turns_under_round_robin`, `a_committed_hosts_run_asks_its_hosts_round_robin`, `a_retried_release_waits_behind_the_other_hosts_and_stops_at_the_cap` and `a_retried_index_keeps_its_host_turn_while_the_other_hosts_releases_are_served` red (mutation 2026-11-17). The re-queue order is `HostQueue::requeue`, which `collect` and the order tests share.
  - `newsvault robots refresh` builds the same profile (`cmd_robots::wire_for`), so its robots.txt fetches to different hosts now leave back to back; same-host spacing is unchanged.
  - Rejected, the shared queue it replaces: the admitted hosts summed in one 10 s queue charged every host for the other hosts' requests; read per host, the refetch worst case put 43,400 s a day, 50.23% of 86,400 s, on each host's bucket with GNW, PRN and CNW, above the bound, and 49,600 s, 57.41%, with the Fed (§11.1's cost-bound construction, every host in one column).
  - Rejected, (b) the per-IP bucket keyed by host: a `<host>.per-ip` file holding the same 10 s as `<host>.per-host`, reserved after that host's own wait, can add at most the time between the previous call's two reservations (not measured), and is a second file per host that a slow-down does not double.
  - Rejected, (c) one SourceId per host: §11.2 refuses a second SourceId per invocation until the run envelope lists `hosts_version` values, so it needs a run envelope, ledger rows and a hosts file per source for the same pacing.
  - **The one place to change it** is `min_interval` in `OpenWebFeed::transport` (`providers/open-web-feed/src/lib.rs`): `Some(INTERVAL)` restores the shared queue; the change also turns `every_golden_page_extracts_to_its_committed_body_under_the_committed_version` red until `extract_version` in `providers/open-web-feed/tests/fixtures/golden_bodies.json` is refreshed, because that version hashes the crate source (2026-11-17).
- **The run's own key, taken by default 2026-11-13.** A run id has a schedule-slot form and an ad-hoc form (`run_id`, `ADHOC`, `RUN_ID_FORMAT` in `services/newsvault/src/cmd_collect.rs`); `run_date` is the UTC date of the run's own instant for BOTH, because no schedule registry exists to take a slot's date from (accepted attack A1.7 asked for the slot's date where there is one).
  - **The one place to change it** is `run_id` in `services/newsvault/src/cmd_collect.rs`.

**The calendar, the listing and the roster are FILES the caller names, taken by default
2026-11-13; robots.txt is a fetched vendor payload, since 2026-11-15.**

- Not a fetched quarter listing: as a hashed input file it keeps a collection reproducible from the files alone and leaves `EdgarPress::listing_url` with no production caller. **The one place to change it** is `cmd_collect::inputs`.
- Required for `edgar_press` and refused for `open_web_wires`, which takes a hosts file instead (§11.2's flag table); which source takes which is `cmd_collect::open_provider`.
- robots.txt is fetched, under attempt rows of its own: `attempts.source` `robots` (`cmd_robots::ROBOTS_SOURCE`), run envelopes of kind `robots_refresh`, phase `Index`, no third `RequestPhase`. A caller-named hashed file, the hosts file, pins its digest (§11.1). The fetch is `newsvault robots refresh` (§11.2).
  - Rejected: a third `RequestPhase`, which forces `classify` and `extract` arms in `edgar-press` and `open-web-feed` that no request reaches. Rejected: source `open_web_wires`, whose `ok` rows with `vendor_rows` 0 would pull down `ok_vendor_rows`' trailing median and appear in that source's ledger rows.
  - The ledger counts only `collect` envelopes in `runs_observed`, `runs_expected`, `runs_unfinished` and the per-source day rows, and takes every kind for the orphan check; the asking clock skips `source = 'robots'`. So a robots 403 is no `holds_a_failure` finding and a robots run fills no missing collect run: `a_robots_refresh_run_is_not_counted_against_expected_runs`, `a_robots_refresh_runs_attempts_are_not_orphans`, `a_robots_fetch_moves_neither_the_asking_clock_nor_a_ledger_check_finding` (mutations 2026-11-15, every envelope counted / `known_runs` from `collect` only / the asking-clock filter removed: each red). Rejected: no envelope, or one in a subfolder: the robots attempts would be orphans and `ledger` would exit 8.
  - `kind` is optional inside `newsvault.run/1`, absent read as `collect` and never written for it, so every earlier envelope and the ledger golden file are unchanged. **The one place to change it** is `cmd_ledger::RunKind`.
  - `source` (PR #52 answer 6, §11.5 step 7 PR 5), `refused`, `wall_s`, `busy[]` and `holds_capped[]` are optional too since 2026-11-18 (S7-D9, S7-D11; §11.5 step 7 PR 4): absent reads as none and each is written only when set, so a `robots_refresh` file and every earlier file are unchanged. **The one place to change them** is `cmd_ledger::Envelope`.
  - `no_registered_source_is_named_robots`: a registered source of that name would vanish from the asking clock.

**The roster: collected first, parsed later (owner decision 2026-11-23; built 2026-11-23, not installed on the VPS).**

- Why now: free sources show only today's company list, so a point-in-time roster (names later delisted or renamed included) cannot be rebuilt later; without it every panel is survivorship-biased (§2 row `universe_version`, the postmortem's +0.80 to −0.86). Snapshots fix this only from the first capture day on.
- Owner rules: raw first (the exact bytes of each daily file with our observation time; tables later); no paid source; robots.txt honoured; no bot protection worked around; the public repository holds no vendor file.
- The memo's `marketvault` context (memo §3) begins here: the roster is market reference data, not news. It lives in the `newsvault` crate and store. Rejected: a crate or store of its own for one file a day (521,795 B); a second store needs a second backup, lease and ledger. That rejection is the roster's alone: filings get their own store (§12, §9). The roster moves to `marketvault` when that context is built (owner decision 2026-11-24).
- Command: `newsvault roster fetch` (`services/newsvault/src/cmd_roster.rs`). Rejected: `collect --source roster`. `collect` drives a `Provider` (`plan`, `classify`, `extract`, the held set, deferral and carry, the schedule's 31 runs); a roster file has no items, and a `Registered` variant reaches every `match` of the ledger and the schedule. `robots refresh` already holds the shape needed: an attempt row and an L2 payload per call, no item rows.
- Files asked, `cmd_roster::FILES` (`the_roster_asks_exactly_sec_s_exchange_file`):

  | file | state 2026-11-23 | why |
  |---|---|---|
  | SEC `company_tickers_exchange.json` | asked daily | free to reuse (SEC webmaster FAQ); cik, name, ticker, exchange; 10,399 rows, 521,795 B, read 2026-11-23 |
  | SEC `company_tickers.json` | not asked | same 10,399 rows and 7,992 CIKs, no exchange column (read 2026-11-23) |
  | Nasdaq Trader `nasdaqlisted.txt`, `otherlisted.txt`, `TradingSystemAddsDeletes.txt` | not asked: owner decision pending | its terms allow "one unaltered permanent copy ... for personal and non-commercial use only"; whether a daily forever archive fits is the owner's call; its bytes never enter this repository, test fixtures included |
  | FINRA OTC Daily List | not asked: owner decision pending | an API key and FINRA's API terms (developer documentation, not fetched) |

- One run: per host, its robots.txt under a `robots` attempt row (`cmd_robots::fetch`, the same row `robots refresh` writes, `hosts_version` NULL); then each file of that host the answer allows, under an attempt row of `source` `roster`, `target_window` the file key, phase `Index`, `live_ingest`; `vendor_rows` is the file's row count; the body and P9's headers as a `payloads` row; no item row. One run envelope of kind `roster_fetch` (`RunKind::RosterFetch`). No retry, no sweep.
  - An error between an attempt's open and its close (a refused pace, a failed blob write) closes that attempt `interrupted` before the run fails, robots and file alike (`cmd_robots::or_abandon`; `robots refresh` too): `an_error_between_open_and_close_leaves_no_attempt_open`. Left open, the next collect's startup sweep closes it and counts it as that collect's interruption, exit 8.
  - Unguarded: a kill, an OOM or a reboot mid-attempt still leaves it open for that sweep, so the 02:00 collect exits 8 for a roster failure; the sweep closes every source's open attempt, by design.
- robots.txt, read with collect's parser (`robots::Robots`), never pinned:

  | answer | the file |
  |---|---|
  | 200 that parses, path allowed, Crawl-delay at most SEC's 100 ms pace | asked |
  | 404 | asked: no rules |
  | 200 whose rules disallow the path | not asked, `robots_disallowed` |
  | 200 that does not parse (an HTML page), or a Crawl-delay over 100 ms | not asked, `robots_refused` |
  | any other answer: 3xx, 4xx, 5xx, transport error | not asked, `robots_unverified` |

  - A file not asked has no attempt row (no call was made) and is named in the report's `files[].not_asked`; the robots attempt row records the look.
  - The reason is on stdout only (the journal on the VPS). The store keeps the robots attempt row and body under the run's `run_id`, from which it can be derived again. `roster show` does not report it: a day robots kept us from the file reads as a day with no roster attempt (open).
  - Nasdaq Trader's `/robots.txt` answered 302 on 2026-11-23, and `Wire` follows no redirect (§3.9), so its files would be `robots_unverified` and never asked. This answers the open question of how our parser treats a 302 to a 200 HTML page: it never sees one.
  - Rejected: a pin in a hosts file as open-web keeps; for one host it adds a file and a refresh step, and nothing extracted here depends on the robots body.
- Pace and contact: `edgar_press::sec_transport()`, now the one home of SEC's transport for both callers; the `Wire` is built with `SourceId` `edgar_press`, so the roster pays into `pace/edgar_press.per-ip` and `pace/www.sec.gov.per-host` with EDGAR (§8 row R19): `a_roster_fetch_through_the_wire_pays_into_edgar_press_s_per_ip_pace`. The User-Agent is the feed contact (`BELLWETHER_FEED_CONTACT_FILE`, the file the VPS mounts); SEC answered it 200 on 2026-11-23; `roster_fetch_reads_the_feed_contact_file_the_unit_mounts` (a dry run with only SEC's variable set is refused). Open: `edgar-press` sends `BELLWETHER_SEC_CONTACT[_FILE]` under the same pace, so the two SEC callers send different User-Agents; unify them before `edgar-press` runs on the VPS. Owner decision 2026-11-24: one contact for every SEC request; `filingvault`, the third SEC caller by design, reads the feed contact and shares one pace directory with both (owner decision 2026-11-25, `FV-Q4`; §12.2). Unguarded: AlphaLens's SEC calls on the same VPS share the IP and not the pace files (§10, ties to AlphaLens).
- Verdict of a file: 200 of the file's shape (`{"fields": [cik, name, ticker, exchange], "data": [...]}`) is `usable`, or `empty` with no rows; 200 of another shape (a challenge page, a changed format) and a body over 8 MiB are `permanent_failure`; 403, 408, 429, 5xx and a transport error are `transient_failure`, as `edgar-press` reads SEC; any other status (404, 3xx) is `permanent_failure`. Every body is kept, failures included.
- Exit, `news_provider::Tally::exit`: 0 every file usable; 7 `vendor_unreachable`; 8 otherwise (`partial_collect`, `vendor_refused_all`). An empty roster counts as a failure: an empty file is the silent zero R6 forbids. A failed robots fetch counts once and its files add nothing; a file robots keeps us from counts as not asked. 2 `credential_contact_missing` before the store is touched; 7 `lease_held`, its envelope finished and marked `lease_held` as a refused collect's is (`a_held_lease_exits_7_and_marks_the_envelope`).
- Reader on a real path: `newsvault roster show --at <instant>`, read-only, no lease. Per file, the newest usable copy whose valid time and observation time are both at or before `--at` (`Visibility::visible_at`):
  - valid time: the copy's `Last-Modified`, else its `Date`; observation time: `attempts.received_at`;
  - a copy received before its own valid time (a server clock ahead of ours) is listed under `refused`, never current, and the read goes on;
  - the copy's `raw_blob`, the sha256 of the file as received, is printed as its `universe_version`;
  - also the newest attempt opened by `--at`, with its outcome and verdict only once it closed by `--at` (else `in_flight` true), so "we looked and it failed" differs from "we did not look" without a verdict learned after `--at`;
  - exit 0 every file has a copy; 1 a file has none; 4 no commit log; 2 an unreadable stored time or header (`roster_show_exits_1_before_the_first_copy_and_0_after`, `a_usable_copy_with_no_readable_valid_time_fails_the_read_by_name`);
  - `current` carries no age: a copy a year old is exit 0. Its age is `at` − `observed_at`, both in the report; a missed day is `NewsvaultRosterMissed`.
- The ledger: a `roster_fetch` run is a known run (no orphan), adds no `runs_observed` and no day row, and `source` `roster` moves no asking clock, as `robots` does not; else a daily SEC fetch would hold `NewsvaultCollectStale` quiet for a dead collector: `a_roster_run_moves_no_asking_clock_and_is_no_collect_run_or_orphan`, `no_registered_source_is_named_roster`.
- Tests, `services/newsvault/tests/roster.rs`; mutations 2026-11-23, one at a time, each red (`cargo test --locked -p newsvault --test roster` or `--test deploy`):

  | mutation | red |
  |---|---|
  | the file's `record` given no payload | `a_roster_fetch_keeps_the_file_as_received_under_one_attempt_after_its_robots` |
  | the envelope written as `collect` | that test and `a_roster_run_moves_no_asking_clock_and_is_no_collect_run_or_orphan` |

  | a failed robots fetch read as no rules | `a_robots_txt_with_no_answer_asks_no_file_and_a_404_asks_it` |
  | the shape check dropped; the field-name check dropped; an empty `data` usable; `empty` counted as work done; 5xx permanent; 429 permanent; any other status transient | `a_challenge_page_an_empty_roster_and_a_403_are_failures_kept_as_received`, each |
  | a transport error returned before the close; a transport error permanent; an over-limit body transient | `a_file_with_no_answer_or_a_body_over_the_limit_is_closed_and_counted`, each |
  | `or_abandon` returning the error without closing the attempt | `an_error_between_open_and_close_leaves_no_attempt_open` |

  | the contact check dropped | `an_empty_contact_and_a_dry_run_ask_nothing_and_write_nothing` |
  | `wire_for` built with `SourceId` `roster` | `a_roster_fetch_through_the_wire_pays_into_edgar_press_s_per_ip_pace` |
  | the observation a day early; the oldest visible copy kept; a failed attempt's body taken as a copy; an `empty` copy taken; the `opened_at` filter dropped | `roster_show_names_the_copy_visible_at_an_instant_by_both_times`, each |
  | the observation taken at `opened_at`; the verdict reported before the close | `roster_show_reports_a_copy_once_received_and_a_verdict_once_closed`, each |

- Schedule: `deploy/systemd/newsvault-roster.timer`, daily 01:20 UTC (§11.5 step 7, units).
  - Rejected: 23:30 UTC for SEC and 13:00 UTC for Nasdaq (the source evaluation of 2026-11-23): both are collect slots, and the store lock refuses a second writer at once (exit 7).
  - 01:20 is inside the 01:18 to 02:00 gap after the 00:30 slot's bound, and 3 h 26 min after the one rebuild time observed: SEC's `Last-Modified` Fri 2026-11-20 21:54:14 GMT, unchanged at Mon 09:02 GMT. SEC's cadence is unknown ("We periodically update the file"); each copy keeps `Last-Modified`, `ETag` and `Date`, so the real cadence can be read from the store after a few weeks.
- Size: 180,362 B gzip on the wire and 521,795 B stored per day (2026-11-23), about 190 MB a year before zstd; L2, kept forever (§3.9).
- What daily copies cannot give: any day before the first capture; a delisting's reason; a name or ticker before the first capture (EDGAR per-CIK submissions carry former names with dates for SEC filers, not fetched); a change inside one day; any security-level id (CUSIP, FIGI).
- One real run, 2026-11-23 09:25Z, from the development Mac into a scratch store, release under review: exit 0; robots `present`, `rules`; the file `usable`, 10,399 rows, sha256 `9551d90d…`, the digest the source evaluation read at 08:57Z; `Last-Modified` Fri 2026-11-20 21:53:43 GMT; pace files `edgar_press.per-ip` and `www.sec.gov.per-host`; `roster show --at` exit 0 naming that copy.
- Unguarded: no test sends the real request to SEC, and the image's TLS to SEC has not run (only on the VPS); a CIK's history across copies is not computed (no reader diffs two copies); the unit has not run on the VPS.

**The vendor's timeouts and body limit, the first an assumption and the second now measured.**

- Timeouts: one unmeasured value, `VENDOR_PATIENCE` in `providers/edgar-press/src/lib.rs`.
- Body limit: 8 MiB, against full daily indexes of **1,057,192 B** / 5,429 filing rows (2026-11-10) and **1,520,327 B** / 7,805 rows (2026-11-12), read as received by `probes/observation_lag/probe.py` on 2026-11-13; the vendor's quarter listing states them as `'1033 KB'` and `'1485 KB'`, rounded to KB, so it is not a source of a byte figure; real rows are 191 to 194 bytes, not the 110 bytes the committed fixture's header carries. **The one place to change them** is `edgar-press`'s `Provider::transport`.
- An answer over the body limit closes `PermanentFailure` and is not retried (§8 row R21).

**The archive's copies: the VPS store is the first copy; the VPS provider's own backup and a daily copy into the owner's Nextcloud on the same VPS stand behind it (N1, decided 2026-11-12 by the owner; amended 2026-11-17, S7-D10 of §11.5 step 7, owner: "zgoda"; amended 2026-11-18, owner: "nie widze sensu trzymania kopii bazy na macOS. VPS jest bardzo reliable", "robmy codzienna kopie na tym samym VPS, ale do folderu Nextcloud - dzieki temu macOS bedzie miec latwy dostep", way A: "zgadzam sie z Twoimi propozycjami"; amended 2026-11-18 to a direct write into the data directory, owner: "a co sądzisz o bezposrednim kopiowaniu plikow do nextcloud? Instancja na VPS jest 'hostem'", then "tak, sprawdz").**

- S7-D10 runs `collect` on the VPS (§11.5 step 7), so the store it writes there is the first copy.
- The VPS provider's backup is the owner's (a few zł a month); its schedule and retention are not read here.
- The daily copy: `deploy/systemd/newsvault-backup` at 22:55 UTC under the store lock writes the files below into the Nextcloud data directory through the AIO container as `www-data` (`docker exec -i -u www-data nextcloud-aio-nextcloud`, `/mnt/ncdata/<user>/files/Backups/bellwether`), then registers the folder with `occ files:scan --path=<user>/files/Backups/bellwether`; the Mac reaches them through Nextcloud's sync client if it syncs `Backups/bellwether` (not checked) (§11.5 step 7 PR 7; "Packs" below, built 2026-11-24, not installed, not run on the VPS).

  | file | holds | written | kept |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `bellwether-vault-log-<UTC stamp>.tar.gz`, the log archive | `newsvault snapshot`'s copy as `commit.sqlite3`, and every other top-level store entry but the live log, its journal, `LOCK` and `blobs` | every night | the 7 newest |
  | `bellwether-vault-blobs-<UTC stamp>.tar`, a pack | the dictionaries and blobs the snapshot names that no pack in the folder holds, each file as the store holds it (raw or `.zst`), under its path relative to the store | a night with at least one such member the store gives | for good: no run deletes one |
  | `<pack>.manifest` | `pack <file name> <bytes> <sha256 of the pack file>`, one `dictionary <sha256>` or `blob <sha256>` line per member, `end <members>` | with its pack | for good |
  | `bellwether-vault-<UTC stamp>.tar.gz` | a whole store, blobs included: what a run wrote before 2026-11-24 | by no run of this script | until the owner deletes it ("Migration" below); no run lists, counts or deletes one |
- The gate's store (owner decision 2026-11-24; built, not installed): the same script with the argument `modelgate`, at 23:30 UTC under the shadow lock, writes `bellwether-modelgate-<UTC stamp>.tar.gz`, the database and every blob it names, into the same folder and keeps its own 7 newest; it is not packed (§3.5, "The store's daily copy", where the reason, the trigger to change it and its restore steps are). A failure of either copy leaves the other's archive, metric and retention untouched.
- The AIO setup, read on the VPS 2026-11-18 (read-only): container `nextcloud-aio-nextcloud`; the data directory `~/nextcloud-data`, `www-data:root` mode 750, bind-mounted on `/mnt/ncdata` inside it; one Nextcloud user, whose id is set only in the VPS's env file (this repository is public); no `Backups` folder yet; the VPS user is in the `docker` group.
- Rejected:

  | alternative | the symptom that killed it |
  |---|---|
  | a pull to the Mac, `rsync` under the store lock (PR 6, 2026-11-18) | owner 2026-11-18: no reason to hold a copy of the database on macOS; Nextcloud's sync reaches the Mac anyway |
  | way A: WebDAV upload with an app password (PR 7 as first built, 2026-11-18) | Nextcloud answers only through a Cloudflare tunnel on the owner's domain, whose request body limit is 100 MB on the Free plan, and locally only as plain http on `127.0.0.1:11000`; it needs an app password file on the VPS; a WebDAV `DELETE` moves the copy to the trash bin, which AIO keeps (`trashbin_retention_obligation` = `auto, 30`, read 2026-11-18), so about 7 + 30 full copies would sit on the disk |
  | writing `~/nextcloud-data` as the VPS user | it is `www-data:root`, mode 750: the VPS user cannot write it; the write goes through the container as `www-data` instead |
  | way C: AIO External storage on a folder this user writes | an AIO reconfigure and a restart of the owner's running Nextcloud |
  | a file copy of the store with no lock | a run committing mid-copy leaves `commit.sqlite3` and the blobs from two moments |
  | the host's `sqlite3` 3.45.1 `.backup` | a second SQLite beside the image's; `newsvault snapshot` runs in the image and links the SQLite the tests link |

- A plain `rm` in the data directory bypasses Nextcloud's trash bin.
- `TimeoutStartSec=1800` bounds snapshot, pack, archive, writes and scan; a store too large for it fails the unit, and `NewsvaultBackupFailed` fires.

**Packs: a blob is copied to Nextcloud once (owner decision 2026-11-24; built 2026-11-24, not installed, not run on the VPS).**

- What was measured, on the VPS 2026-11-24, read-only, by the owner's session (the commands are not recorded here):

  | kept whole-store archives, by night | 137 MB (11-19), 211 MB (11-20), 223 MB (11-21; 223,343,293 B, 4,334 items, read 2026-11-22), 161 MB (11-22), 228 MB (11-23) |
  | the store directory | 397 MB after 6 days |
  | of it, the commit log | 28 MB |

- Arithmetic from those six days, not a measured trend; it takes the 369 MB that is not the commit log as blobs (the split between `blobs`, `items`, `runs` and `policy` is not measured) and ignores gzip:

  | shape | copies of a blob on the disk | copies of the log | growth a day | days to 33 GB |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | whole-store archives | 10: the store, 7 kept, the work copy and the hidden copy during a run | 10 | 66 MB (397 / 6) × 10 = 660 MB | 50 |
  | packs | 2: the store and one pack; that night's new blobs twice more during a run | 10 | 61.5 MB (369 / 6) × 2 + 4.7 MB (28 / 6) × 10 = 170 MB | 194 |

- The planned archive of annual reports is a store of its own, `filingvault` (§12), about 4.26 GB for its initial fill (an estimate, §12.9; its primary documents alone 1.96 GB at 19.7× on 43 documents): the whole-store shape would keep 8 copies of it in the folder, and its fill waits for packs (§12.9). How that store's blobs are copied is not designed (§12).
- The unit of copy is one pack a night. Rejected:

  | alternative | the symptom that killed it |
  |---|---|
  | one file per blob | argued from the script, not measured: each file costs a `docker exec` to write, one to rename and one `occ info:file`, and `occ files:scan` walks the folder every night; 9,093 blobs for 4,334 items (the drill below) is 2.1 blobs an item, so 8,543 items in 6 days is about 3,000 files a day and 1.1 million a year in one folder the Mac's sync client would also list |
  | whole-store archives, fewer kept | n kept still costs n + 3 copies of every blob |
  | a state file on the host listing what is packed | a lost state file packs everything again without saying why, and a lost pack is never noticed |
  | the manifest written first | a run killed before its pack leaves a manifest naming a pack that never existed, and every later run alerts until a person deletes it; pack first, the leftover is a pack nothing names and the run goes on |

- Component placement (owner rule 2026-11-24: code goes in the component that owns the responsibility):

  | piece | owner |
  |---|---|
  | which blobs and dictionaries a commit log names; where each file is in the store; reading one back to its digest; a `.zst` file's dictionary; the pack's layout and its sha256; the manifest's format; which manifests count; which members are still to pack; which of them the store cannot give, and why (`not_packed`); whether the folder's packs hold all a log names (the restore's check, `--dry-run`, exit 1 when not) | `newsvault blobs pack` (`cmd_pack`, `BlobStore::stored_file`) |
  | the consistent copy of the commit log | `newsvault snapshot`, unchanged |
  | whether a restored store is sound | `newsvault blobs verify`, unchanged |
  | docker, the units' lock, the folder's listing, each pack's length and sha256 as the container's `wc` and `sha256sum` print them (the data directory is `www-data:root` 750, so no `newsvault` container reads a pack), carrying the manifest files out with the container's `tar`, writes through the container, renames, `occ`, metrics, the 7 newest, its own work directory | `deploy/systemd/newsvault-backup` |
  | the one store name the script still knows | `blobs`, beside `commit.sqlite3` and `LOCK`, in the list of top-level entries the log archive leaves out |
  | the folder's file names: `<pack>.manifest` is built by `cmd_pack::MANIFEST_SUFFIX` and matched by the script's globs and retention pattern | both; rejected 2026-11-25: the manifest's name as a report field. Symptom: the script lists, stages and cleans the folder by name shape before any report exists (the two reads, the `.part` leftovers) |
  | no dictionary in the log archive | rejected 2026-11-25 as a second copy of each dictionary (36 KB and 70 KB in the review's store). Symptom: the script would name `blobs/dictionaries`, a store path only the binary knows |

- How a run knows what is packed: it reads the folder, and no state is kept on the host. The script hands `newsvault blobs pack` one `<pack> <bytes> <sha256>` line per pack file (`--have`), a directory holding every manifest under its own file name (`--manifests`), and the snapshot (`--log`). A manifest's pack is the file name without `.manifest`.

  | the folder holds | `blobs pack` | the run |
  |---|---|---|
  | a whole manifest, and its pack at the length and the sha256 the manifest states | its members are held | exit 0 |
  | a manifest whose pack is absent, of another length or of another sha256; a manifest that is not whole: no `end` line, cut mid-line, a line of another shape, another member count, another pack's name, not UTF-8 | names the pack in `lost`; packs its members again | writes the night's files and the metric, deletes the oldest log archives beyond 7 and a killed run's `.part` files as on any night, no pack and no manifest, exits 8 |
  | a pack no manifest names | names it in `unrecorded`; packs whatever the log names that no held manifest lists | the same, exit 8 |
  | a line of the listing that is not three words | `input_unparseable`, exit 2 | exits 2, nothing written; the script writes the listing itself |
  | a blob or dictionary the snapshot names that no pack holds and the store lacks, or that does not read back to its digest (owner decision 2026-11-25) | leaves it out and packs every other member; names it in `not_packed` (`kind`, `digest`, `reason`: `absent` or `digest_mismatch`) and by one `newsvault.error/1` line on stderr (`input_absent` or `input_unparseable`, the digest in `message` and `details.digest`); writes no pack and no manifest when the store gave no member; exit 8 | the same as a lost pack: the night's files, the metric and the retention, then exit 8 |

  - `not_packed[].reason`: `absent` when the member's file, or the dictionary its `.zst` file names, is not in the store; `digest_mismatch` when one of the two is there and does not read back to its digest (an altered payload, a file that is no zstd frame, a dictionary of other bytes). For a blob left out over its dictionary the stderr line's `message` names the dictionary.
  - A member in `not_packed` is in no manifest, so every later night finds it still to pack and reads it again: exit 8 each night while the store cannot give it, and the night the file is back it is packed and the run exits 0. No state and no code path of its own; `a_named_blob_that_is_gone_or_altered_is_named_and_left_out_until_the_store_gives_it` runs the three nights.
    - The repair is a person's: no command re-creates a blob. `blobs verify` on the live store names the same digest; a refresh of the item re-fetches a page only if the source still serves the same bytes.
    - Any other failure of a read (`io_failed`: a permission, a disk error) still ends the run with exit 2 and nothing written.
  - Exit 8 for a pack repeats every night until a person removes the pair `lost` names or the pack `unrecorded` names; the script deletes neither, and `NewsvaultBackupFailed` stays firing over any later cause of exit 8. The repair, by the owner's yes:

    | step | what | go on when |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1 | one night has run since the report first named the pack | that night's report shows `pack` not null, or `packed` 0 |
    | 2 | restore runbook steps 3 to 5 against the newest log archive | step 5 exits 8 with `packed` 0: every member is in a pack that counts |
    | 3 | `docker exec -u www-data nextcloud-aio-nextcloud rm -f -- "<dir>/<pack>" "<dir>/<pack>.manifest"`, then `php occ files:scan --path=<user>/files/Backups/bellwether` | the next night exits 0 with `lost` and `unrecorded` empty |

  - A blob already in a held pack is not read again, so a blob the store loses later stays restorable from its pack.
  - A pack whose bytes changed at the same length is `lost` the next night and its members are packed again from the store (review of PR #79, 2026-11-25: one bit flipped in a 580 KB pack was counted as held, exit 0, and in a dictionary member left 171 of 350 blobs unrestorable). Each night therefore reads every pack once through `sha256sum`: 369 MB after the first run, 369 + 61.5 × 194 = 12.3 GB on the day the table above reaches 33 GB, which fits the 1,800 s bound alone at 6.8 MB/s (12,300 / 1,800); the VPS's read rate is not measured.
    - Trigger, set before any run: the nightly run's seconds, read from the journal, above 900 (half the bound): hash on one night a week. No rule reads it.
    - Not detected: one hex character of a manifest's `blob` line changed to another. That member is packed again, exit 0, naming nothing (review harness, 2026-11-25).
  - A pack and its manifest both gone leave nothing in the folder to name: the night packs their members again from the store and exits 0 (review harness, 2026-11-25: `packed` 8, exit 0). With the store gone too, restore step 5 exits 1.
    - Rejected: each log archive carrying the pack names its night saw, compared the next night. Symptom: the state the host file was rejected for, moved into the folder.
  - A blob or dictionary lost from the store before any pack holds it (owner decision 2026-11-25): the night packs what the store gives, writes the log archive and exits 8 naming the member. Rejected:

    | alternative | the symptom that killed it |
    |---|---|
    | stop by name and write nothing (built 2026-11-24, exit 4 or 2) | one lost blob ends every later backup, the log archive included, until a person repairs the store: a copy of everything but one blob is worth more than no copy |
    | the script reading the report to word its message per cause | it would parse JSON in `sh` and learn the report's fields; it maps the binary's exit 8 to one message that points at the report above it |
    | the retention skipped on such a night | the lost-pack night already runs it; after 7 unrepaired nights every kept log archive names the member, and each older archive names fewer rows, not more blobs |
- Dictionaries are members: every `dictionaries` row of the snapshot that no pack holds is packed before the night's blobs, and so is a dictionary a packed `.zst` file names in its header when the log has no row for it. A blob's dictionary is in its pack or in an earlier one; the log archive holds none.
- Order of one run, and what a run that ends early leaves:

  | step | what | ended here, the folder holds | the next run |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | `newsvault snapshot` into the work directory | nothing new | starts again |
  | 2 | the folder created, each pack's length and sha256 read, the manifests carried out as one tar and unpacked into the work directory | nothing new | starts again |
  | 3 | `newsvault blobs pack` writes the pack and its manifest into the work directory, without the members the store cannot give; neither file when it gave none | nothing new | starts again |
  | 4 | the log archive: `tar -czf` | nothing new | starts again |
  | 5 | pack, manifest and archive each written as a hidden `.<name>.part`, its byte count compared | on SIGTERM or an error the `EXIT` trap removes each; after SIGKILL, the OOM killer or a reboot they stay, and Nextcloud's scanner skips `.part` | packs the same members again and, in its retention step, deletes every `.part` of the three shapes |
  | 6 | renamed: the pack | a pack no manifest names | names it `unrecorded`, packs its members again, exit 8 until the repair above |
  | 7 | renamed: the manifest | a pack and its manifest, no log archive of that night | counts the pack as held; the older log archives restore with it |
  | 8 | renamed: the log archive | all three | nothing to repair; the first `occ files:scan` registers them |
  | 9 | scan, `occ info:file` of each new file, the metric, the retention | all three | as before 2026-11-24 |
  | 10 | exit 8 when step 3 exited 8 | all three, or the log archive alone; with a member in `not_packed`, a log archive naming a blob no pack holds | reads that member again: packs it, exit 0, or names it, exit 8 |

  - Every log archive under its final name therefore has, in the folder, a pack for each blob and dictionary its log names, except those a night's report named in `not_packed` and no later night packed (2026-11-25; before, without exception). Restore step 5 over such an archive exits 1 and names each in `not_packed`.
  - The work directory `~/.cache/bellwether/backup-vault.*` (the gate's: `backup-modelgate.*`) is on the same disk and holds the snapshot, the listing, the manifests, the night's pack and the log archive; a run ended by SIGKILL leaves it, and the next run of the same store removes it before it makes its own (2026-11-25). The units start one run of a store at a time; a second run started by hand beside the unit's loses its work directory and exits 7 or 2.
- Retention: "the 7 newest" counts log archives only. No pack is deleted, so every blob a kept log names stays in the folder.
- The lock: the unit's `flock --nonblock` on the store lock for the whole run and `TimeoutStartSec=1800`, both unchanged, so the run's bound stays 23:26:30, before the 23:30 slot (§11.5 step 7 PR 7). `blobs pack` takes no `LOCK` lease: it reads files that never change, named by a snapshot already taken.
  - The first run after the install packs the whole store: one pack of at most 369 MB (2026-11-24). It reads every blob and writes that many bytes through `docker exec`, which every nightly run did before, without gzip and with one read-back of each blob (`blobs verify`: 9,093 blobs in 3 s on the VPS, 2026-11-22). From the second night on a run reads every pack once more for its sha256. Not measured: either's seconds.
  - Killed at the bound: systemd's SIGTERM runs the trap, nothing is recorded, `NewsvaultBackupFailed` fires and the next run packs the whole store again. A store whose first pack cannot be written in 1,800 s fails every night; no flag splits a pack.
  - The annual-report fill is not this store's (§12): about 4.26 GB over about 6 nights (§12.9), and no pack of it is designed or measured against the bound.

  |---|---|---|
  | `newsvault_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds` | the run's start, written once the whole-store archive is looked up | the run's start, written once every file of the night is looked up; also on a run that exits 8 for a lost or unrecorded pack or for a member in `not_packed` (2026-11-25): the stamp says the night's files are in the folder, so `NewsvaultBackupStale` stays quiet and `NewsvaultBackupFailed` alone fires |

**What the drill compares, and what the 156-of-156 does not say.**

- (1) `probes/parity_baseline.py` hashes (sha256) the sorted distinct **vendor ids** (lake `id`, §3.1's `source_item_id`), **not** `item_id` (§2, produced only in the new archive), so it shows the id **set** came back and would match with every title, body and url different.
- (2) It agreed on **156 of 156** days, re-derived 2026-11-12, over a corpus with none of the shapes the two readers can disagree on (across 779 run files and 243,226 rows: zero null ids, empty-string ids, null publication or ingest times and inverted rows; no file missing `tickers`), so `unusable_rows` and §5's rows 4 and 5 have never fired on real data and the number says the lake is clean, not that two readers encode one rule.

**The comparator exists since 2026-11-13**, which closes the third thing that was not true of it and makes the first two measurable rather than merely admitted.

- `newsvault day` emits a `content_digest` beside the `id_digest` (`lake::Day::content_digest`), so a matching id set with a different title no longer passes; `probes/newsvault_parity.py` computes both in pandas, compares every reported field day by day and exits 1 on any difference, under a decision rule registered before it ran (`probes/newsvault_parity/PREREGISTRATION.md`, which holds its run log).
- Committed corpus, 9 partitions and 11 run files, one partition per shape the lake lacks: null id; real empty-string id; null publication time; null ingest time; inverted row at both precisions; re-stamped repeat; repeat arriving with an earlier observation; day-dated value beside an instant one; run file missing a column. Its first run disagreed on exactly one of them and the reader changed (row R3).
- **CI runs no Python**, so the gate is the probe's committed output: `services/newsvault/tests/parity.rs` is the only reader of `expected.json`.
- Not covered: the corpus is synthetic rather than a sample; both readers read the same parquet bytes through two arrow bindings; the new archive's own rows have no second reader.

**The risk the owner accepted, stated rather than implied.**

- The VPS store, the provider's backup and the Nextcloud copies sit in one provider and one account, the Nextcloud copies on the store's own disk: a kernel or a bad deployment is covered by the Nextcloud copies, a disk by the provider's backup; a billing, suspension or credential loss is covered only by the Mac's Nextcloud sync client, if it syncs `Backups/bellwether` (not checked). A copy at a second provider was the alternative and was not taken.

**Freshness: 2 hours inside the US session, 6 hours outside it (N2, measured 2026-11-12).**

- The alert is the age of the newest item (§5's "a consumer is silently dead" row), measured over the predecessor's lake (156 partitions, 779 run files, 243,226 raw rows, publication times 2026-05-19 to 2026-11-10) as gaps between consecutive publication instants over **61,282** distinct items.
- **61,282** is the union of distinct `id` values across the archive, because a gap is a property of the archive, not of a partition; memo §5.1's **62,507** is the per-partition count summed, double-counting 1,225 repeats of 501 ids (row R3's grain); both re-derived 2026-11-12 in one pass.

| window | p50 | p90 | p99 | p99.9 | worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13:00–20:00 UTC, the US session | 1.0 min | 10.1 min | 26.7 min | 50.3 min | **1.2 h** |
| outside it | 0.3 min | 13.0 min | 45.0 min | 105.1 min | 332.6 h |

**What would have fired is not what that table says.**

- A gap's quantile is bucketed by the hour it **starts**, while the alert asks whether the newest item's age exceeds the threshold at an instant inside the window, so a gap from 12:10 to 15:00 UTC is an out-of-session gap and an in-session alert. `probes/news_gap.py` prints both, measured 2026-11-12:

| episode | gap | 2 h in session | 6 h outside |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-19 → 06-02 | 332.6 h | fires | fires |
| 06-02 → 06-03 | 16.8 h | fires | fires |
| 06-03 12:10 → 15:00 | **2.8 h** | fires | does not fire |
| 06-05 → 06-08 | 93.2 h | fires | fires |

- All four start outside the session, which is why gap-start bucketing reports zero in session; the control reproduces that zero. **The threshold choice survives**: three of the four are outages the 6-hour rule catches anyway, so 2 hours adds one alert in 175 days, 2026-06-03's.

**What makes those two numbers wrong.**

- They measure the predecessor's **retrieval** coverage, not the world's news, so a different vendor moves them; provisional, re-measured against `open-web-feed` (§11) and the first real vendor.
- The publication gap transfers where an observation gap would not, because the predecessor's `ingested_at` spacing is its scheduler, not the news; the record already holds outages: 161 of the 175 days hold an item, 14 hold none, and the 332.6-hour gap is one.
- The alert is not built: `ledger` computes the newest item's age (`freshness.publication_clock`), and none of the 8 families `newsvault.prom/1` exports carries it.
- Before its rule is written, both thresholds are re-measured on `open_web_wires` data (owner, 2026-11-22): the open-web feed adds about 158 items a day (2026-11-21, one Saturday), against about 61,282 over 175 days here, so the 6-hour rule may fire every night and weekend.
- Unguarded until then: a host whose index lists 0 rows all day. `NewsvaultRowsZero` fires only when a vendor listed rows and none committed (`cmd_ledger.rs`, `row.rows_committed == 0 && row.vendor_rows - row.held > 0`), and `NewsvaultCollectStale` reads the age of the last request, not of the newest item.

| G2 scans every non-hidden file outside `target/`, as `version.rs` skips hidden entries, and reads its exemptions from `.gitattributes` | a fixed list of digested paths (PR review 2026-11-16): the hosts entry removed and the hosts file converted to CRLF left all 425 tests of 3 crates green; a hard-coded exemption list: a second copy of `.gitattributes` | same file |

**Owner decisions of 2026-11-22, the Snapshot; each stands where its fact is.**

| decision | where it stands |

| 1, the L1 text is in the data file | §3.0, data |

**Defaults taken by the builder on 2026-11-22, `cut`, not by the owner.**

| default | rejected, and why | where it is changed |
|---|---|---|
| two passes of 512-row reads | one read transaction over both passes: the store sets no `journal_mode` (rollback journal, grep of `store.rs` 2026-11-22), so a read held across a year's body reads would lock out `collect`'s commits | `cmd_cut::CHUNK_ROWS`, `each_row` |
| row groups closed at 64 MiB of encoded bytes, ZSTD at its default level | parquet's defaults (§3.0); no level or bound was measured | `snapshot_contract::ROW_GROUP_BYTES`, `writer_properties` |
| `open_attempts` reported, the cut not refused | a refusal: blocks every cut while `collect` runs, and `--through-seq` already reproduces the cut | `cmd_cut::open_attempts` |
| a body's presence checked in the first pass; a body altered on disk found in the second, its staging directory removed | hashing every body in both passes: reads a year's 2.3-3.9 GB twice | `cmd_cut::select` |
| `staging_left`, never removed by `cut`, for a staging directory an earlier cut left | removing any `.tmp-<id>`: a concurrent cut of the same set loses its staging directory | `cmd_cut::CutError::StagingLeft` |
| `seq_high_water` required in `panel.manifest/2` | optional within version 1: a manifest omitting it loses the rebuild bound exactly when the snapshot is lost | `panel_contract::FIELDS` |
| the validator ignores a manifest field it does not know | refusing it: a later optional field would be refused by an older validator | `snapshot_contract::validate` |

**Open since 2026-11-22.**

- How often to cut and how long to keep a cut: unset, and needed before any timer; cuts are cumulative (§3.0's size table).
- `SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT body_blob) FROM items` on a backup copy: unrun; it decides whether one body file shared across cuts saves space.
- Decision i (takedown): a cut is an L1 copy outside `vault`, and nothing records where cuts were written.
- Before deploying, the new build's `items --at <now>` once on a backup copy: run 2026-11-22, `items --at 2026-11-22T18:00Z` exit 0 on the restored copy (V2 below); how many rows the old reader dropped silently is still not counted.
- Every `newsvault` command, found 2026-11-22: an argument that does not parse (`cut --at nonsense --format json`) writes `usage error: <text>`, not the `newsvault.error/1` object, and no command takes `--json` as an alias of `--format json`.
- `publish` segments still use parquet 60.1.0's writer defaults (`publish.rs`, `ArrowWriter::try_new(.., None)`): no compression, up to 1,048,576 rows a row group held in memory.

**Vault definition of done (owner decisions of 2026-11-22; states read 2026-11-22).**

- `derive`'s code starts now, on the committed fixture and on local cuts; no threshold below blocks it.
- Three thresholds:

  | threshold | criteria |
  |---|---|
  | 1, `vault` runs unattended | V1, V2, V4 and the disk criterion |
  | 2, `derive` on production data | V3 |
  | 3, `vault` complete | C2, C3, C4 if `derive` asks for it, and the N2 freshness alert |

- V5 runs alongside `derive` and is in no threshold; a failing day pulls work back to `vault`.
- Disk criterion: the VPS's free space read and an alert on it, or an accepted risk recorded in N2. State: met (owner decision 2026-11-23).
  - Free space read 2026-11-22: 63 GB free of 193 GB (`df -h`, root filesystem, the one the store, a staging copy and 7 backups share, N1).
  - The alert is the VPS's shared host rule `LowDiskSpace` in `~/monitoring/prometheus/alert.rules`: `node_filesystem_avail_bytes / node_filesystem_size_bytes * 100 < 15` for 5m, routed to the same Telegram receiver; read on the VPS 2026-11-22.
  - Not in this repository: the rule belongs to the shared monitoring stack (§11.5 step 7, "Alerting"); none of the 23 rules in `deploy/prometheus/newsvault.rules.yml` (17 before the shadow's four of 2026-11-23 and the gate copy's two of 2026-11-24) reads disk, and `newsvault-monitoring-check` does not check the shared rule.
  - The store's growth: N1's "Packs" table, six days read 2026-11-24; not a measured trend.
  - Design, no code: the filings store's initial fill is about 4.26 GB in one copy (an estimate, §12.9), and waits for the backup change because 9 copies of it do not fit (§12.9).
- A missed `collect` day is mostly recovered late with a later `observed_at`, so it gives no cutoff inside that day: the PRN sitemap walk reads back to its last basis (sitemap depth about 70.5 h, measured 2026-11-17) and the GNW id walk to the highest id of the previous RSS read (§11.2). Lost as `live_ingest`: items of RSS-only hosts (the Fed, CNW) and of any outage longer than a host's list depth. Not tested on a real outage.

**V4 (c): what tells the owner that Prometheus or Alertmanager is down (options for the owner, 2026-11-22; nothing built).**

| option | catches | misses | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) an external dead man's switch: an always-firing rule (`expr: vector(1)`) routed with a short `repeat_interval` to a free external check service as a webhook; the service messages the owner when the pings stop | Prometheus, Alertmanager or the route down; the VPS down or offline | an outage of the service; the service's free-tier limits and channels were not checked | an owner account at the service; its ping URL in `alertmanager.yml` only (a secret: never in this repository); a 16th rule and a second bellwether route |
| (b) a bellwether systemd user timer on the VPS reading `/-/ready` of Prometheus and Alertmanager and sending to Telegram through the Bot API directly | Prometheus or Alertmanager down or not ready | the VPS down (the timer stops with it); a route that drops alerts while both are ready | the bot token and chat id readable by the deploy user; a second sender beside Alertmanager; a script, units and their tests |
| (c) accept the risk in N2 | nothing | a dead stack is seen only when someone looks | an owner line in N2 |

- Recommendation: (a). It is the only option that catches a dead VPS, and it adds no bellwether code beyond one rule and one route; the account is the owner's step.
- (b) shares the VPS's failure and puts the chat's credentials in a second place; (c) leaves every case of the first row open.

- Left out of every threshold: CNW admit or drop (§11); usage errors outside `newsvault.error/1` (above); `publish` segments on parquet defaults (above); R15's leak in `items` and `publish` (§8); no title column (§3.0).

**Optional projects, outside `vault` (owner rule 2026-11-22: `bellwether` is independent of AlphaLens, the predecessor; no commits to AlphaLens; its data is optional input and never a threshold).**

- A copy of the predecessor's outputs (parquet files only, never its Postgres mirror): optional; not started.
- An import of the predecessor's lake as `bulk_dataset`: optional; a separate project with these open problems:

  | `observed_at` | no rule yet; whether a run's `run=<stamp>` is its start or its end is not checked |
  | attempts | the lake has no attempt rows, so "nothing happened" and "we did not look" cannot be told apart; 14 of its 175 days hold no item |
  | producer | `bulk_dataset` has no producer (§8 row R10) |

**Ties to AlphaLens still open (2026-11-22).**

- The VPS's monitoring stack `~/monitoring` was set up by AlphaLens in May 2025 and is shared with other projects; bellwether's three touchpoints in it are `deploy/monitoring/` and the rules (§11.5 step 7, "Alerting"); the rest of its config is not in this repository.
- AlphaLens's alerts: muted since 2026-11-22 at the owner's request, by a child route to the receiver `blackhole`; its timer still rewrites `alphalens.rules` hourly.
- `newsvault day` defaults its lake root to the predecessor's lake path (`lake.rs`, `main.rs`).
- `services/newsvault/Cargo.toml` and `lib.rs` describe the crate as "for AlphaLens".
- AlphaLens on the same VPS calls `openrouter.ai`, `data.sec.gov` and `www.sec.gov` and none of the open-web hosts (its journal, last 3 days, read 2026-11-22); an `edgar-press` run from the VPS would share SEC's per-IP budget with it while it runs; `newsvault`'s pace files do not see another process's calls (§8 row R19).

| term | meaning |
|---|---|
| **POC** | proof of concept: the first build |
| **Target** | the shape the crate grows into; nothing in it is built or gated |
| **Held** | the store already has an answer for a story, so the feed does not fetch it again |
| **Admitted** | a hosts-file row with status `admitted`: its robots.txt allows the paths used and the host passed a probe |
| `Index` request | a dated news sitemap or RSS feed |
| `Document` request | one article page |
| GNW / PRN / CNW / BI / Fool | GlobeNewswire / PR Newswire / Canada Newswire (`www.newswire.ca`) / Business Insider / The Motley Fool |
| Fed | the Federal Reserve press feed (`www.federalreserve.gov/feeds/press_all.xml`) |
| Yahoo | Yahoo Finance's news sitemap (`finance.yahoo.com/news-sitemap.xml`) and its article pages |
| provider key | the path segment after `https://media.zenfs.com/en/` in a Yahoo sitemap row's `image:loc`: the source Yahoo files the row under (§11.2) |
| keyed / direct index | Yahoo's index, read under a key filter; and each other admitted index (§11.2's cross-check) |

    - The scan's first version was itself quadratic: the same 2 MiB page took 346.6 s, because each tag searched the open stack for `svg`/`math`; each entry now carries that count.
    - The count is meant never to fall below html5ever's depth less the implied `html` and `body`: an end tag closes its element only when it is on top or below implied-end elements (`p`, `li`, ...) alone, and is otherwise ignored, as html5ever ignores an end tag naming no open element; raw text is skipped except inside `svg`/`math`; a comment ends where html5ever ends it (`<!-->`, `--!>`); a `>` inside a quoted attribute does not end a tag. `depth::tests::each_rule_of_the_scan_counts_its_own_row`, 17 rows; 14 mutations 2026-11-15, one per rule: 14 red; the stray-end-tag rule's mutation (the implied-end elements popped although the name is not open): red on its 2 rows.
    - Before that rule (review 2026-11-15, release build, one run each): `<rb><rt></x>` repeated 16,000 times (192,000 B) counted 2 while html5ever held 32,002 and parsed in 1.78 s; `<ul><li></x>` × 300 counted 301, html5ever 602. Both now count 600 for 300 rounds.
    - `a_page_nested_past_the_bound_is_unusable_and_one_at_the_bound_is_read` (mutations 2026-11-15, the check removed: red; `>=` for `>`: red).
    - Unguarded: html5ever's reconstruction of active formatting elements adds nodes no source tag opens. Probe 2026-11-15: 800 rounds of `<p><b x=i>t</p>` (13,490 B) built 322,004 nodes, depth 804, in 0.154 s; the scan counted 1,600 and refuses it, but no general rule bounds that reconstruction.
    - Sloppy markup (`<span><b>x</span>`) counts deeper than html5ever's tree, so a real page could be refused.
