- Every UTC day is collected, weekends included. Investor-relations pages are never fetched. Observation time is `Wire`'s `received_at`: `an_open_web_run_collects_a_globenewswire_day_end_to_end`, whose stub receives one second after it sends (mutation 2026-11-15, `collect` observing at `requested_at`: red; green before the stub told the two apart). The store refuses an observation time set by the provider: `Committer::rows_of` in `cmd_collect.rs`, `StoreError::LiveItemPlacedItsOwnObservation`, `a_live_row_that_placed_its_own_observation_is_refused`.

| host | valid time |
|---|---|
| PRN, GNW, Fed | RSS `pubDate`, `ValidSource::VendorPublished` |
| CNW | sitemap `news:publication_date`, a full instant with offset, `ValidSource::VendorPublished`; built 2026-11-17 (rules table above) |
| CNBC | the page's `article:published_time`, `ValidSource::OurExtraction`; never its sitemap (§11.6) |
| Yahoo | its syndication time field, `ValidSource::VendorPublished`; the field is named in its host PR: built 2026-11-17 as the sitemap's `news:publication_date` (rules table above), `Z` with second `00` on 2,017 of 2,017 followed-key rows of the 26 polls of 2026-11-16. Same minute as the wire's own feed, matched by normalised title, distinct Yahoo urls of the 26 polls (Python, 2026-11-17): `business-wire.com` 28 of 28 against BW's RSS; `prnewswire.com` 339 of 391, 15 later by more than 5 min (at most 90), 32 earlier |
| Fool, BI | the sitemap's publication field, `ValidSource::VendorPublished`; the field is named in their host PR, as Yahoo's is |
| never | `lastmod`, `dateModified`, fetch time, a date folded into midnight |

- `ValidSource::PageMetadata` stays unbuilt.
- **`ValidSource` per host, decided 2026-11-15 by the owner.** Both arms exist (`provider.rs:41-46`); `CollectedItem.valid_source` is required (`provider.rs:147`); since 2026-11-17 CNW, Fed and Yahoo items are built `VendorPublished`; no item from Fool or BI is built yet.
  - `VendorPublished`: a value read from a structured feed field the publisher states (RSS `pubDate`, sitemap `news:publication_date`, a sitemap's publication field, Yahoo's syndication time field; that field is the sitemap's `news:publication_date`, named 2026-11-17).
  - `lastmod` stays excluded (the `never` row), so only a sitemap's publication field is `VendorPublished`, and a sitemap with no publication field gives no valid time.
  - `OurExtraction`: a value read out of an article page under a hashed rule (CNBC's `article:published_time`).
  - Rejected: `OurExtraction` for sitemaps, because the arm would then mean "we parsed XML" and no longer separate "the publisher stated it" from "we inferred it from the page".
- Bot protection (HTTP 403, a challenge page, a web application firewall, DataDome) is a `PermanentFailure`, never retried in another form.
- robots.txt is respected; a robots.txt 404 is recorded as "no robots" and is not digest-pinned. Sites' terms of use are not a criterion (owner, 2026-11-14; reaffirmed by the owner 2026-11-19 after a terms review).
  - Pages fetched 2026-11-19.
  - PRN and CNW: one Cision terms of use, `https://www.prnewswire.com/terms-of-use/` ("Last Updated: September 1, 2023"), forbids "any robot, spider, site search/retrieval application, or other manual or automatic device".
  - Yahoo: `https://legal.yahoo.com/us/en/yahoo/terms/otos/index.html` forbids collecting data "using any automated means … including but not limited to robots, spiders, scrapers".

- Pace: `interval = max(Crawl-delay, 7 s)` (owner decision 1, 2026-11-19, §10); a host may be slowed, never sped up. Busy time of one host = its summed paced waits plus its request times; worst case ≤ 50% of a day per host (owner decision 1, 2026-11-17, §10). The stop deadline caps the run's wall time (§11.2); `collect` serves hosts round-robin since 2026-11-17, so the refetch worst-case poll takes 700 s of waits, not 966 s, while no host holds a `Retry-After` (§10's round-robin table; 7/10 of the 1,000 s and 1,380 s computed at 10 s on 2026-11-17).
  - Built: one `per_host` of 7 s (`INTERVAL`) for every host and no per-IP pace, so each host is its own queue (§8 row R19 hole 7; §10). Since 2026-11-16 (owner decision 1) a host whose `*` Crawl-delay is above it is refused by `collect`; per-host intervals (§11.3) are the path for such a host.

- Held is keyed on (SourceId, `story_id`) over every target window, never the run's window alone.

| story state | held? |
|---|---|
| has a committed item | yes |
| `Document` attempt closed `Usable`, `Empty`, `PermanentFailure` with no 3xx status, or `Usable` with only unusable rows the page decided | yes (an `Empty` or unusable page: its raw blob is linked by the attempt's `payloads` row for an attempt closed at user_version 6 or later, and is a file no row names before it (§3.9), and no re-extraction reads it, P11 not being built; a re-fetch of a PRN, CNW or GNW page that yielded text gave the same extracted text, on PRN and CNW in other bytes (§3.9), and no `Empty` or unusable page was re-fetched); `a_document_that_yielded_only_unusable_rows_is_not_fetched_again` (`NoArticleBody`, the page-decided control) |
| `Document` attempt closed `Usable` with an unusable row the index row decided (`attempts.listing_unusable` > 0) | no (owner decision 2026-11-15, §10): no rule reads the page's own time for a listed row (GNW's `page_valid` dates only a request with no listed value, a walked id, §11.2), and the listed pubDate is kept only in the index attempt's raw blob and, since 2026-11-16, the document attempt's `payloads.listed_date` (§3.9), which no rule re-reads (P11 not built), so only a refetch lets a later listing or a corrected pubDate rule (days 1-9, above) reach the story; `a_document_whose_listed_time_did_not_parse_is_fetched_again_and_committed_once_the_listing_parses`, `a_usable_document_with_a_listing_unusable_row_holds_nothing_and_a_v3_or_page_one_holds`. Cost: fetched by every poll while the index lists it with the bad value, `a_story_whose_listing_stays_unparseable_is_fetched_by_every_poll` (3 polls, 3 fetches); counted per source and day by `ledger`'s `listing_unusable` (§8 row R4); bound below |
| `Document` attempt closed `PermanentFailure` with a 3xx `transport_status` | no (owner decision 2026-11-15, §10): a redirected release is fetched again by the next poll, so step 5's refusal of redirects (§11.2) does not hold it forever; `a_document_answered_with_a_redirect_is_fetched_again_by_the_next_poll` (a loopback server's 301 through the real open-web `Wire`, its target never sent, §8 row R21), `a_redirect_whose_body_is_over_the_limit_is_fetched_again_by_the_next_poll` (the same 301 with a body over `BODY_LIMIT`, below), `a_permanent_document_answered_with_a_redirect_holds_nothing_and_one_with_no_status_holds` |
| `Document` attempt closed `PermanentFailure` with its body stored cut (`payloads.truncated` 1), while the limit in force is at most the cut's length | yes (owner decision 2026-11-20): a fetch at the same limit repeats the same cut |

- Built 2026-11-18 (§11.5 step 7 PR 4): `SLOTS` in `services/newsvault/src/schedule.rs` is the one home of this table: 31 slots, each a UTC hour and minute with its window's period.
  - No field carries an offset; every instant is built in `Utc`.
  - `Schedule::new` refuses, each by name (`each_broken_table_is_refused_by_name`): no slot; a slot outside 00:00–23:59; a slot named twice; slots out of order; a period whose half is not longer than the patience; a period equal to neither the gap from the slot before nor the gap to the slot after.
  - The committed table passes (`the_committed_schedule_is_a_schedule`): 23:30's 90 min is the gap from 22:00, 00:30's the gap to 02:00.
  - Kept in `newsvault`, not in `open-web-feed`: `extract_version` hashes every file of `open-web-feed/src`, so a schedule change there would read as an extraction change.
  - Readers: the stop deadline below, the GNW walk's frontier cutoff (the start of `--at`'s slot, §11.2's GNW row), and the test holding `crosscheck::LONGEST_POLL_PERIOD` to its longest period (`the_cross_check_lead_is_the_committed_schedules_longest_period`).
- A run's slot: the latest slot start at or before the clock's `now` when `collect` starts (`Schedule::slot_at`), the day before's 23:30 for a run before 00:30.
  - A slot start is its own slot, 1 µs before it the slot before (`a_run_belongs_to_the_latest_slot_start_at_or_before_it`).
  - 00:00 and 00:10 belong to the day before's 23:30, 10:59 to 09:30 (`the_23_30_slot_and_the_09_30_slot_cross_their_gaps`).
  - The clock, not `--at`: `--at` 18:59:30 started at 19:00:30 takes the 19:00 slot's 19:14:30 stop (`the_slot_and_the_wall_time_come_from_the_clock_not_from_at`).
  - A dry run reports the slot of the clock's `now` too, whatever its `--at`; with an `--at` a live run refuses (another UTC day, after the clock) that stop can precede `--at` (PR #52 contract review F4, kept as the stop a live run started then takes).
- The deadline: `SlotAt::deadline`, `min(start + period / 2, next) − patience`; the patience is the provider's `timeouts.global`, open-web's `VENDOR_PATIENCE`, 30 s.
  - The next slot binds in no committed slot; a synthetic 90-min slot 30 min before the next one stops at the next one less 30 s (`the_next_slot_caps_a_half_period_that_would_pass_it`).
- Default: an `open_web_wires` collect with no `--deadline` takes the schedule's (`Registered::on_schedule`); `--deadline` overrides it, for tests and manual runs.
  - The envelope's `deadline` and `slot` (`start`, `period_s`, `next`) state it; `slot` is null when `--deadline` was given (`with_no_deadline_an_open_web_run_stops_at_its_schedule_slots_deadline`).
  - EDGAR is not on this schedule: an `edgar_press` run with no `--deadline` has none (`an_edgar_run_with_no_deadline_takes_none_from_the_schedule`).
- A run started more than half a period late belongs to its slot and gets a deadline already passed: it takes the lease, asks nothing, writes each planned request as a `deferred` row `run_deadline` and exits 8 (`a_run_started_past_its_slots_deadline_asks_nothing_and_defers_every_index`: 10:15:00Z, 6 index requests, 6 rows).
  - Rejected: a named error before the lease: the store would hold no row of the slot, so "we did not look" would read like a run that never started, and S7-D5's carry would have nothing to read.
  - Rejected: `DeadlineNotAfterNow`, as for a given `--deadline`: exit 2 means a usage error, and the timer's unit would read failed.

A document is read under the rule whose `valid_format` reads its listed value (`OpenWebFeed::rule_of`), so a sitemap follow-up is dated by `news:publication_date` and an RSS one by `pubDate`. `open` refuses a paged index not ending in the query pair `page=1` (`PagedIndexNotPageOne`), read under a rule that is no news sitemap (`PagedIndexNotASitemap`), or whose rule and the row's own read one probe value alike (`IndexFormatsOverlap`).
        - Rejected: a request field naming the index that listed a document: every `Request` literal and the `payloads` row would carry it, while today a stored document is re-read from its url and `listed_date` alone.
        - Hole: a sitemap row with no readable minute is read under the RSS rule, so its unusable row names `pubDate` as its field.
      - One story per release: both rows key through `item_key`. Replayed 2026-11-17 over probe10's 48 RSS and 49 sitemap bodies through the committed feed's `story_of` (a temporary test, not kept): 438 RSS stories, 744 sitemap stories, 417 in both, the counts §11.6 states from the probe's own keys.
      - In one run, a story an earlier index issued counts as held when a later index lists it (`news_provider::collect::attempt_once`), so a release both list is fetched once, from the RSS, which is asked first; its `listed_date` is the RSS's and its ObservationTime is that document fetch's. When the sitemap names a ticker for it, the RSS's follow-up moves ahead in PRN's lane (§11.5 step 7's ticker-first bullets).
      - Paging (`paging::next_page`): page N+1 is an `Index` follow-up carrying, as `listed_date`, the listed value of page N's oldest row, and it is planned only when all hold:
        - a basis was handed (none: `first_poll`, page 1 only);
        - page N holds no basis key;
        - page N's oldest row is not older than the basis's oldest row, a tie going on; pages list newest first: 0 rows newer than the row before them over probe10's 49 pages, 4,900 rows (Python, 2026-11-17);
        - page N's oldest row is not newer than page N−1's, a tie going on;
        - its url is allowed by the host's pinned robots (§11.1's per-document check).
        - Rejected: a tie as a stop: one minute can fill a page of 100 rows; 107 releases were listed at 09:00 ET on 2026-11-17, 98 of them on 14:10Z's page 1 (PR review, probe10, 2026-11-17).
        - No page count is read and no cap is fitted: the walk ends at the basis, past the basis's oldest minute, at a page newer than the one before, or at a page answered empty or not usable.
        - Rejected: the sitemap index `sitemap-news.xml` (19 pages listed on 2026-11-14, 12 at 08:16Z and 23 at 20:26Z on 2026-11-17: research and probe 11, §11.6) as the cap: one more request per poll, and no request carries its count to the page that would need it. A fixed page cap: a fitted number.
        - Open item, not changed (owner, 2026-11-19): since 2026-11-19 15:30 UTC every deadline-bound run left page 2 unread (`next_page_unread`), because page N+1 is queued behind page N's document follow-ups; ticker-first keeps that place.
          - A page-2 deferral is never carried and never closed: `Committer::open_deferred` reads `document` rows only (`services/newsvault/src/store.rs:1636`–`1648`, `d.phase = ?2` bound to `RequestPhase::Document`), so `carry` (`news-provider/src/collect.rs:842`) never sees it and `close_uncarried` (`collect.rs:907`–`927`) never closes it `expired`; `deferred_index_requests_are_never_carried_or_closed` pins this.
          - So it never raises `NewsvaultDeferredExpired`: `newsvault_carried_expired` counts `deferred_closed` rows (`services/newsvault/src/cmd_ledger.rs:797`–`805`, `1595`; `deploy/prometheus/newsvault.rules.yml:50`–`51`). It stays an open `deferred` row, counted once in its day's `deferred` `run_deadline`.
          - Not measured at 7 s: how often page 2 is now reached.
        - Past its last page PRN answers 200 with an empty `urlset` (probe 11, §11.6): `Empty`, so the walk ran out and the poll is `no_previous_key`, a basis, and the run exits 0. It is reached only when the basis is older than the sitemap's depth, 70.5 h on 2026-11-17 (research). Test: `a_poll_whose_next_page_is_past_the_end_ran_out_and_is_the_basis_of_the_next`, over the real page-24 body.
      - Continuity (`paging::continuity`, after the run in `cmd_collect::continuity_of`):
        - `first_poll` with no basis;
        - else `next_page_unread` when the last page holds no basis key and `next_page` plans a page after it that was not read usable: it failed, or robots disallow it. It wins over a broken boundary, so a poll that read less than it planned is never a basis.
        - else `boundary_no_shared_key` when two neighbouring pages share no key; else `complete` when the last page holds a basis key.
        - else `no_previous_key`, the walk having run out: no next page was due, or the next page answered `Empty` (`Committer::empty_index_pages`).
        - Recorded on the poll's page-1 attempt (§3.2's `continuity`), in the envelope's `continuity` and counted by the ledger.
      - Generation label (`paging::generations`, owner decision 2026-11-17): each boundary whose two pages share no key gets one `Generation` from both pages' `x-sitemap-generated-at`, read as RFC 3339 instants and compared to the millisecond (`Generation::between`):

        | label | stamps | what it says of the gap |
        |---|---|---|
        | `same_generation` | equal | pages of one generation join exactly, so no row fell between them |
        | `older_generation` | the later page older | a real gap |
        | `newer_generation` | the later page newer | rows may repeat; still no key shared |
        | `generation_unknown` | absent or not RFC 3339 on either page | nothing |

        - The label only describes the gap. It never decides `complete` against a gap, nor the basis; both stay with the shared-key rule. With the header dropped by PRN every label is `generation_unknown` and the rest is unchanged.
        - `Last-Modified` is not read: on 3 of 3 probe-11 responses it is the stamp cut to the second, so two stamps inside one second would read as equal.
        - Stored as four counts beside `continuity` (§3.2's `boundary_*`), in the envelope's `continuity[].boundaries` and on the `continuity` human line, and summed by the ledger (`boundaries`, human `boundary_<label>`).
        - Rejected: labels derived at ledger time from `payloads.headers`: the ledger would re-read and re-parse every page blob under the rules to find which boundaries share no key. One row per boundary in a new table: its page column would have no reader.
      - Basis (`Continuity::is_basis`): the newest poll that read every page it planned, so every continuity but `next_page_unread`, a broken boundary included (owner decision 2026-11-17, option B, "zgadzam się" to the PR #47 review's F1), read before the lease (`store::basis_pages`, blobs by digest; a missing blob is `BlobAbsent` and refuses the run).
        - The cost accepted: a broken boundary's stretch stays recorded on its poll (`boundary_no_shared_key`, labelled) and the sitemap walk never looks for it again; probe10's 13:51–13:59Z stays unread, 14:15Z being `complete` at page 1 against 14:10Z's two pages (§11.6's replay). Its remedy is the monthly archive (PG-D5, a later PR).
        - Rejected: a broken boundary as no basis (PR #47): the next poll walks back to an older basis across more pages and boundaries, each able to break again. Over the research's 12-page pass of 2026-11-17 08:17Z, with the basis at page k = 2..12, all 11 walks were `boundary_no_shared_key`, 2 to 11 pages (§11.6's pass table); once no basis replaces it the walk grows to the sitemap's last page. A broken stretch stored as a minute interval and closed by a later poll: proposed, not chosen (owner decision 2026-11-17).
        - Rejected: complete polls only: an empty store's first poll is never complete, so no poll would ever anchor, and a basis gone from the sitemap would make every later poll walk every page.
        - Rejected: `no_previous_key` whatever ended the walk, an unread page included: 14:10Z with page 2 answering 503 three times became the basis, and 14:15Z read page 1 only and was `complete` while 13:51–13:59Z stayed unread (PR review, a temporary test, 2026-11-17).
        - Unguarded: `complete` assumes a release newer than a row already seen is listed above it. Over probe10 at a 5-min stride, 35 keys first appeared on page 1 below a row an earlier cycle saw; 19 of the 20 printed were dated before that row (cycle 28: 15 rows at 09:00–09:01 ET at rows 17–99, below a row at 09:02) (PR review, stride.py, 2026-11-17). At 5 min all 35 were on page 1; at 30 or 90 min such a row on a page below the one holding the basis key is missed while the poll reads `complete`. Remedy: the monthly archive, a later PR; no page margin is fitted.
        - A run committing between this read and the lease leaves an older basis, which reads more pages, never fewer.
        - `basis_pages` reads a store at user_version 10 to 14, because the run migrates the store after it (`a_v10_to_v14_store_keeps_its_basis_for_the_run_that_migrates_it`). Rejected: this build's version only: the first run after the step to 11 read no basis and recorded `first_poll` (PR #48 review, a temporary test, 2026-11-17).
      - PG-D6: an RSS release no sitemap page lists stays an ordinary RSS item (`a_poll_whose_page_one_overlaps_the_first_poll_is_complete_and_reads_one_page`). Its absence is derivable from the stored RSS and sitemap payloads; no field reports it (not built).
      - The plan check is per (day, url) since 2026-11-17 (the conformance bullet below); a next page is no vendor row of the page that planned it.
      - Not built: the Yahoo cross-check reads PRN's RSS alone as PRN's direct index, so a release only the sitemap listed can still be named unlisted.
      - Probe10 and the research's 12-page pass replayed through the committed code: §11.6's replay tables. Tests and mutations: §11.5 step 6's PRN completeness.

        - `open` refuses a url that does not expand to one release on the row's host (`IdWalkNotARelease`), and a row whose rule keys no story by release or reads no page time (`IdWalkRuleNotReleaseKeyed`).
      - Rules: `gnw` gains `story_key: release` (§11.1's `item_key` bullets) and `page_valid` (`meta[property="og:article:published_time"]`, `content`, `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`); a `page_valid` format that prints no second is refused.
      - Range (`Walk::range`), read before the lease by `cmd_collect::ranges_of` through `store::walk_read`:
        - through: the highest id, any language, of the newest usable answer of the index, the previous poll's frontier (PG-D2); the current poll's own answer never raises it.
        - after: the id the newest basis poll walked through (`attempts.walk_through`); when that basis walked nothing (`first_poll`), the lowest id its own answer lists, less one.
        - none, so `first_poll` and no walk, when the store holds no usable answer of the index or no basis poll; a store below user_version 12 holds no basis, so the first run after the step is a first poll.
        - unknown, so `range_unread` (`WalkPlan::RangeUnread`) and no walk, when the store holds both and the previous answer, or a basis that walked nothing, lists no release on the walked host (a changed link shape): no `walk_through`, no basis, so the next poll walks from the same basis. While the shape stays changed every poll is `range_unread`, counted by the ledger.

          - Unguarded: the in-run filter, and walked stories added to the issued set. The feed already leaves out an id its own answer lists and one index per host is walked, so removing either turned no test red; nor did issuing the walk only when the index matched a row (PR #49 review, 2026-11-18).
      - Answered (`store::answered_urls`): a document attempt closed `usable`, `empty` or `permanent_failure`, a 3xx included. A 3xx is not held (§11.1's held table): a listed row is fetched again by the next poll, the walk never asks that id again.
      - A walked page is dated by the minute holding its `og:article:published_time` (`minute_containing`): `valid_raw` keeps the second, `valid_field` is `og:article:published_time`. With no readable time it is `NoParseableValidTime` decided by the page, so held. Its ObservationTime is the instant its fetch returned, as for any live document.

Rejected: any document with no listed value: an RSS row with no `pubDate` was dated by its page while one with an unreadable `pubDate` was refused (PR #49 review, 2026-11-18).

Any other 3xx stays `PermanentFailure` (§10).

EDGAR has no walk and reads no frontier.

Not counted: a planned request, an `Index` follow-up (PRN's next sitemap page), a walk id (`Extracted::walk`) and a retry (§8 row R21).
    - An `Index` follow-up is outside the cap because the worst case above already counts index requests apart from it. Rejected: counting it; a cut page 2 leaves its poll `next_page_unread`, no basis, so the next poll cannot join either (§11.2's PRN completeness row).
    - A retry asks the same follow-up again, so it is never a new one. Rejected: counting each retry; a host answering 503 would spend up to 3 of the cap's slots per follow-up and push other hosts' follow-ups past the cap.
  - The 301st counted follow-up, and every one after it, is a `deferred` row with reason `follow_up_cap` and is never sent (§3.2); the run exits 8 `partial_collect` (S7-D8, §5.1).
  - First run on an empty store, a projection (arithmetic 2026-11-18, the queue simulated in Python: one lane per host, round-robin, the cap counted at pop; PRN's sitemap index takes one turn before its follow-ups; re-run 2026-11-19 at the cap of 300, the same simulation reproducing the 150 rows first):
    - inputs: GNW RSS 20, PRN sitemap page 1 100 plus 0 to 20 RSS-only releases (in-run dedup, `issued`), CNW 100, the Fed 20 (§11.2's index sizes, 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-16), Yahoo 141 followed rows at p1500 (2026-11-16); a first poll walks no GNW id (`first_poll`).

      | case | follow-ups | deferred | PRN | CNW | Yahoo |
      |---|---|---|---|---|---|
      | five hosts, Yahoo at p1500 | 381 to 401 | 81 to 101 | 14 to 34 | 13 | 54 |
      | four hosts, no Yahoo key row | 240 to 260 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — |
      | S7-D6's row: PRN by its RSS alone, 20 | 301 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

    - GNW and the Fed lose nothing in each case: their 20 are issued within the first 20 rounds.
    - The last row is reproduced by `news_provider::collect::tests::the_global_cap_cuts_one_of_yahoos_first_run_follow_ups`; the other two rows are not tested.
    - The queue alone: S7-D3's deadline is not simulated. On waits alone at 7 s it cuts a lane past 125 requests: in the last row Yahoo's index and 140 asked follow-ups are 141, so the deadline defers at least 16 more of Yahoo's; request times cut earlier.
    - The next run carries each deferred story (S7-D5, §3.2's `deferred_closed`).
  - A story is added to the run's `issued` set when its index is read, before the queue decides to ask or defer it, so a second index of the same run listing a deferred story (PRN's sitemap beside its RSS) drops it and writes no second `deferred` row; since 2026-11-18 it counts `held` only once the run asked it (§3.2's `held`).
  - Counted too since 2026-11-18: a carried follow-up that is no walk id (S7-D5, §3.2's `deferred_closed`).
  - Busy time against the stop deadline and this cap is projected, not measured, and a lower bound: the completeness cost bullets above (round-robin, 2026-11-17); §11.6's weekday probe busy-time table (2026-11-16) is the serial sum from before round-robin.

|---|---|
| sources | every candidate that passes robots and a weekday probe, incl. Business Wire if stable (its Earnings feed on 2026-11-16: §11.6; no stability threshold is fixed), Zero Hedge, Newswire.com (measured zone, date-only valid time) |

| per-host intervals | R19 hole 7 closed (`HostPaces::Listed`); the path for a host whose Crawl-delay is above 7 s, refused until then (owner decision 1, 2026-11-16) |
| redirects | followed as their own paced, ledgered requests; today `Wire` follows none for any provider (open-web since 2026-11-15, edgar since 2026-11-16), which closed R19 hole 9 by refusing; `Location` kept since 2026-11-17 (§3.9's P9 row); needs `Document`-phase follow-ups |
| robots | re-fetched on a schedule; a changed robots digest blocks the host until the hosts file is updated. Built 2026-11-15 without the schedule and wider than a host: `robots_refused` refuses the whole run (§5.1) |
| collectors | per SourceId in parallel; needs a startup sweep that tells live runs from dead ones; then the lease covers only `Committer::reserve` through COMMIT (§6) |
| follow-up cap, run length | run length: S7-D3's construction; cap: 300 since 2026-11-19, set against that day's counted new documents per run (S7-D6, §11.2's cap bullet); busy seconds in every collect envelope and run file since 2026-11-18 (S7-D11), summed per day by the ledger; no live run has measured them, so only a projection exists (§11.2's cap bullet) |
| PRN and GNW completeness | every release named per poll (PRN sitemap pages, built 2026-11-17) or per id (GNW walk, built 2026-11-17), and per month (PRN archive, not built): §11.2's completeness table |
| `NoArticleBody` share per host | a ledger reading; its threshold is fixed before its first measurement |
| outbox poller | wakes `derive` and feeds the private stream (memo D-7) |

     - the lag from a `pubDate` minute to the feed listing it is one point, not a distribution: all 26 polls of 2026-11-16 answered `Last-Modified: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 21:15:18 GMT` (one ETag, one body sha256, Cloudflare `HIT`), 18 s after the newest item's `pubDate` 21:15:00 GMT (bcreg20261113a). `Last-Modified` is when the file changed, not when a client could first read it. No new item was listed that day; the 20 items span 2026-09-25 to 2026-11-13, so a release stays listed for weeks (window 1,176.75 h, §11.2).
     - a `pubDate` with a zero-padded day is `NoParseableValidTime` and fetched by every poll while listed; never observed (0 of 9 single-digit days, 2026-11-16).
     - release text that names a person is stored as it stands: enforcement20261112a names the individual the action is against (P3; r removes addresses only). Media contacts are `div` cells and are not read; a release that puts them in a `p` would store names and numbers, as on PRN and CNW (decision r).

7. VPS timer, follow-up cap with the run deadline, busy seconds in the envelope.
   - Hard gates before the first live run; the robots one built 2026-11-17, condition A's core 2026-11-18 (PR 3), its deadline computed from §11.2's schedule since 2026-11-18 (PR 4), S7-D5's carry 2026-11-18 (PR 5):
     - Owner condition A (2026-11-16, "zgadzam sie na warunek A"): step 7 MUST build the run-window cap before the first live run. A host whose `Retry-After`, or doubled wait, ends past the run window is stopped, and its remaining planned requests are recorded as not looked.
       - Built 2026-11-18: `newsvault collect --deadline <RFC 3339>`, after `--at` and, on a run that is not `--dry-run`, after the clock's instant (S7-D2: `--at` may lie in the past), or `invalid_argument` (exit 2: `a_deadline_not_after_at_is_a_usage_error_and_a_later_one_reaches_the_envelope`, `a_deadline_the_clock_has_reached_is_refused_even_after_at`); absent, every request is asked as before. `collect` asks `Exchange::reserve` before `AttemptSlot::open`; a slot opening after the deadline answers `Reservation::PastDeadline { go_at, by_server }` with no attempt row, no pace or hold stamp, no wait and no ordinal; that request and the rest of its host's lane, walk ids and `Index` pages included, are `deferred` rows; other hosts keep their turns, and each reaches its own stop when the deadline passes for it, a url no host keys included.
       - A counted follow-up stopped at the deadline gives its cap slot back (`HostQueue::stop`), since it is never asked: `collect::tests::a_follow_up_stopped_at_the_deadline_spends_no_cap_slot`. Before, with GNW stopped on its first follow-up under a cap of 2, PRN's second was deferred `follow_up_cap` after one follow-up asked (review probe 2026-11-18).
       - The reason split: `host_held` when the profile's own `per_host` from the host's last grant opens by the deadline, so a hold or a doubling moved the slot past it; `run_deadline` otherwise, a hold or a doubling included (`a_slot_the_profiles_own_pace_opens_after_the_deadline_is_run_deadline`); at the boundary, the profile's own slot opening exactly at the deadline, it is `host_held` (`a_hold_past_a_deadline_the_profiles_own_pace_meets_exactly_is_host_held`). Rejected: `host_held` whenever a hold or doubling is in force: a deadline the run's own pace already missed would raise S7-D8's `host_held` alert for a cut that was not the server's.
       - The deadline is inclusive: a slot opening at it is asked, one opening 1 µs after it is not (`a_slot_opening_exactly_at_the_deadline_is_asked_and_one_microsecond_later_is_not`).
     - A per-document robots check, owner decision 2026-11-17 (~16:10Z, "zgoda"): each document url's path is checked against its host's pinned robots before it is asked, read as robots decision 4 (2026-11-17) reads a path (§11.1).      | S7-D2, what the deadline measures | the run's wall time | busy time summed over hosts: cuts runs about 4× earlier; a deadline per host: a run can still hold the lease when the next slot starts, giving exit 7 and an unfinished run file |
     | S7-D3, the deadline | `min(slot_start + period/2, next_slot) − VENDOR_PATIENCE` (open-web's, 30 s, `providers/open-web-feed/src/lib.rs`), the slot read from the schedule as data (§11.2's table); built 2026-11-18, §11.2's schedule bullets | process start + period/2: 50.03% of a day in the worst case (31 runs with one last request running its 30 s), and a catch-up start more than period/2 late (more than 15 min in a 30-min slot) runs into the next slot |
     | S7-D4, "not looked" | a `deferred` table (run, host, url, phase, story_id, listed_date, reason in `run_deadline`, `host_held`, `follow_up_cap`) plus a ledger count | an attempt row with no call: breaks §8 row R16, one attempt row per HTTP call; the envelope only: a JSON file cannot feed S7-D5, and "nothing happened" and "we did not look" must differ in the store |
     | S7-D5, deferred items | carried: the next run puts each unresolved deferred item the store does not hold into its host's lane, behind every request of this run on that host, oldest `deferred_at` first (fresh-first, owner decision 1, 2026-11-19); one older than 24 h is closed `expired` | re-listing only: PRN's and GNW's next poll shared no item in 18 of 25 pairs (§11.2); the front of the lane, ahead of the index (as PR 5 built it): a missed index loses a whole period's listing and the GNW frontier; behind the index and ahead of its follow-ups (owner decision 2026-11-18, "tak"): run `open_web-20261119T143004Z` fetched 0 fresh PRN stories while the cap, then 150, went to Yahoo 61 + GNW 20 + PRN carried 69, and 155 PRN listings were deferred `follow_up_cap`; promotion of a carried item near its 24 h expiry: not built; the interval and the cap it waited on were set on 2026-11-19 (§10's per-host interval, §11.2's cap bullet), and expiry under them is not yet measured (the S7-D5 expiry bullets below this table) |
     | S7-D6, the follow-up cap | 300 since 2026-11-19 (owner decision 2; 150 before, §11.2's cap bullet), global, counted at issue in round-robin order; an explicit exception (owner decision 2026-11-17 ~21:30Z, "tak", option A): the GNW walk's ids are outside the cap and the walk has no cap of its own, bounded by its id range and by S7-D3's deadline (unreached ids `deferred`, S7-D4, and carried, S7-D5), because at the US peak the walk needs about 52–72 requests per 30-min poll (probe10: frontier +566 ids in 3 h 55 min) and round-robin by host already keeps GNW from starving the other hosts; §11.6's 30-min replay walked up to 113 ids in one poll | ⌊300/5⌋ = 60 per host: on a first run's 301 follow-ups (20 + 20 + 100 + 20 + 141 Yahoo rows at p1500) CNW loses 40 and Yahoo 81, against 0 and 1 under the global cap (arithmetic 2026-11-19; at 150: 30 per host, 70 and 111 against 55 and 96, and the critique's four-host case, before Yahoo: 37 per host, CNW loses 63 against 10, 2026-11-17; four hosts at 300: 75 per host, CNW loses 25 against 0, 2026-11-19) |
     | S7-D7, a server's hold | persisted in the pace file, capped at 24 h, with an alert above it; the pace file then holds a grant no call used, the opposite of §10's rejected "grant earlier than the call" | memory only: asks a held host again every run; uncapped: `Retry-After: 315360000` silences the host for 10 years |
     | S7-D8, the exit | every reason exits 8 `partial_collect` (§5.1); the collect unit sets `SuccessExitStatus=8`, so a failed unit means newsvault's 2, 4 or 7, the store lock's 7, the NTP check's 1, or docker's 125 (a missing image, a container left holding the name); its `ExecStopPost` writes the unit's result and exit status, and `NewsvaultCollectFailed` fires at the next rule evaluation (PR 7; with no rule reading the unit, a failed unit was seen as `NewsvaultCollectStale` 3 to 4 h later or `NewsvaultRunsMissed` the next day, PR #54 review, 2026-11-18); an hourly `ledger --check` watchdog alerts on `host_held` and `expired` counts; built in PR 6 as `ledger --format prometheus` textfile metrics and the rules in `deploy/prometheus/newsvault.rules.yml` (bullets below) | exit 0 for a cut: hides a lost tail; exit 8 as a unit failure: the unit would read failed on most peak runs |
     | S7-D9, overlap | a run refused `lease_held` rewrites its run file with `finished_at` and `refused: lease_held`, and the ledger leaves it out of observed runs; no `Restart=`; `TimeoutStartSec` = the longest deadline + 2 min; built 2026-11-18 but the systemd half: `cmd_collect::run` and the ledger's `runs_lease_held`, whose run still counts toward its day's `runs_expected` (`a_run_the_lease_kept_out_finishes_its_run_file_refused_lease_held`, `the_ledger_sums_busy_time_against_half_a_day_and_leaves_lease_held_runs_unobserved`, whose lease-held file alone states 3 expected runs); a lease-held run whose run id already has a run file puts that file back byte for byte and writes no mark (`a_lease_held_run_puts_back_the_run_file_its_run_id_already_had`; PR #52 mutation review F3: a finished run's file was rewritten `lease_held` and left the ledger's observed runs); the systemd half built in PR 6: no `Restart=`, `TimeoutStartSec=2790` derived from `schedule.rs` (§11.2's longest-window bullet), and a timed-out run's container removed by `ExecStopPost` | skipping the run file: breaks `cmd_collect.rs`'s rule that it is written before the lease, so a run that never gets one is a record |
     | S7-D10, deployment (option C, owner 2026-11-17 ~19:00Z) | CI builds an OCI image from a version tag `v*` and pushes it to GHCR; systemd user timers run it with `docker run --rm --name newsvault-collect`, the fixed name refusing a second container while an orphan stands; the store, pace files included, a bind-mounted volume; the contact a read-only mounted file named by `BELLWETHER_FEED_CONTACT_FILE`; the image named by tag and digest in `~/.config/bellwether/newsvault.env`; an NTP check before each run; a manual first `robots refresh` before go-live; no `RandomizedDelaySec`; a Kubernetes CronJob manifest kept in the repo and validated, not deployed; the VPS store is the first copy (N1, §10) | build on the VPS from a tagged clean clone and run the tests there: rustup, `libsqlite3-dev` and a compile beside AlphaLens on the VPS, and a later move to Kubernetes (the owner's plan) needs an image anyway; `/etc/bellwether/env` mode 640 holding the contact: `docker inspect` prints an environment value |
     | S7-D11, busy seconds | an additive `busy` object in `newsvault.collect/2`, per host: waited, requesting, requests, stopped, not_looked, held_until, doublings, plus `wall_s`; `wall_s` and per-host `busy_s` in `runs/<id>.json`, summed by the ledger against 50%; built 2026-11-18, the bullets below | stdout only: nothing on a real path reads it |

       - At cap 300 and 7 s (2026-11-19), day runs have room too: a row deferred at 14:30 also gets the next day's 11:00–14:00 runs before its 24 h expiry, so the "only if" no longer holds; not re-measured.

         | order | Yahoo follow-ups per night run | rows closed `expired` |
         |---|---|---|
         | fresh-first | ≤ 10 | 0 |
         | fresh-first | 20 | 949 |
         | 2026-11-18 order (carried ahead of the follow-ups) | 20 | 0 |

     - S7-D11, built 2026-11-18 (PR 4):
       - Envelope `busy`, null for a dry run: `wall_s`, and per host `host`, `waited_s`, `requesting_s`, `busy_s`, `requests`, `stopped`, `not_looked`, `held_until`, `doublings`; the owner's names, with `_s` on the durations as `wall_s` has it; one `busy` human line and one line per host.
       - `waited_s`: the clock inside `Exchange::reserve`, a stopped reservation's included (`news_provider::collect`).
       - `requesting_s`: each answer's own `received_at`, or `failed_at`, less its `requested_at`, read by `Wire` either side of the socket.
       - `busy_s` = `waited_s` + `requesting_s` (§11.1 Pace); the send gate's wait (§8 row R19, since 2026-11-22) is in neither, since it falls after `reserve` and before `requested_at`: `busy_s` leaves it out (probe 2026-11-22, a second send 1.07 s owed at the gate: 8.93 s inside `reserve`, 1.07 s between `opened_at` and `requested_at`); its bound is R19's added-wall-time bullet; `wall_s` = the clock at `cmd_collect::run`'s start to the run file's `finished_at` (`the_slot_and_the_wall_time_come_from_the_clock_not_from_at`).
         - Not counted: `open_provider`'s reads before `run` (basis, walk, `answered_urls`), and the run file's `started_at` is `--at`, so `finished_at − started_at` is not `wall_s` (PR #52 contract review F5).
       - `stopped`: the deadline stopped the host's lane; `not_looked`: the host's `deferred` rows, every reason.
       - `held_until` and `doublings`: `Wire::slowed`, the latest hold the run's `Wire` read or raised while it was still ahead of the clock, and the host's doublings in this run (`a_wire_reports_each_hosts_doublings_and_the_hold_it_saw`; a hold read from an earlier run's pace file: `a_wire_reports_a_hold_an_earlier_run_left_beside_the_store`).
       - Run file (`newsvault.run/1`): `wall_s`, `busy[]` (`host`, `busy_s`) and `holds_capped[]` (`host`, `retry_after`, `held_until`; owner decision 2026-11-18, answer 1), and since PR 5 the collect's `source`; each optional (§10's run-file bullets).
       - Ledger day row: `wall_s`, `wall_share` of 86,400 s, `busy[]` per host with its `share`, `holds_capped`, `runs_lease_held`; the report's `busy_bound`, 0.5; `--check` findings `wall_time_over_bound` and `host_busy_over_bound` above 0.5, never at it; a `busy` human line per day and a `busy_host` line per host.
       - Tests: `every_busy_field_reaches_the_envelope_the_run_file_and_the_ledger`, every field a value no other field has (waited 21 s, requesting 9 s, busy 30 s, 3 requests, stopped, 1 not looked, held, 2 doublings, wall 36 s); `the_ledger_sums_busy_time_against_half_a_day_and_leaves_lease_held_runs_unobserved`.

       - S7-D5's lane order (owner decision 1, 2026-11-19, fresh-first): each lane of `HostQueue` holds two queues.
         - `fresh`: the planned index, the follow-ups it lists, the next sitemap page, walk ids and retries, in the order pushed; a retried carried request goes to the back of `fresh`.
         - `carried`: filled by `HostQueue::carry`, oldest `deferred_at` first; `pop` serves it only while the lane's `fresh` is empty.
         - Exception to "this run's follow-ups are fresh": a carried story the run's own index lists again is not pushed to `fresh`; it stays in `carried` and is asked once, after this run's fresh requests on its host (its story is in `issued` from the run's start; `a_relisted_carried_story_stays_carried_and_is_not_issued_twice`).
         - Fresh-first holds per lane: a lane whose `fresh` is empty serves `carried` on its own turn while other lanes still hold fresh requests, and a counted carried request takes a cap slot there (`a_lane_out_of_fresh_requests_asks_its_carried_one_in_its_own_turn`).
         - Round-robin across lanes and counting at `pop` are unchanged; `HostQueue::stop` defers `fresh`, then `carried`.
         - Its gain is read as §8 row R22's `listing_latency`, fresh and carried apart; no production number yet (2026-11-19).
       - Ticker-first (owner decision 3, 2026-11-19): inside a lane, a fresh `Document` follow-up whose index row names a listed company is asked before one whose row names none; each group keeps its listing order.
         - Built as slots: each fresh `Document` follow-up pushes a `Slot::Document` into `fresh` and itself into the lane's `named` or `unnamed` queue; `pop` fills a slot from `named` first. The planned index, the next sitemap page, walk ids, retries and carried requests keep the places they were queued at, and `HostQueue::stop` defers in the order `pop` would have asked.
         - Producer: `Request::names_ticker`, never sent, outside `filter_params` and never stored; set by `OpenWebFeed::index_rows_of` from `parse::IndexRow::names_ticker`.
           - Counts over the 62 index blobs of 2026-11-19 09:36:50Z–20:30:18Z (the store's, read 2026-11-19, Python ElementTree):
           - news sitemap: a non-empty `news:news/news:stock_tickers`; PRN: 345 of 1,065 unique sitemap urls (25 fetches of pages 1–4), never blank;
           - RSS: an unprefixed `category` whose `domain` ends with `/rss/stock` and whose trimmed text is non-empty (`parse::rss_rows`); GNW files `Exchange:SYMBOL` under that domain and ISINs under `.../rss/ISIN`; GNW: 86 of 301 unique items (18 polls), every item with a stock-domain category; every ticker category stood first in its item and none held surrounding whitespace.
           - Rejected: the text pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z .&-]*:[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$` on the trimmed text, ignoring `domain` (proposed with ticker-first, 2026-11-19): on the same 18 polls it named 83 of the 86, missing 3 items (2 stories, one in two languages) whose symbols hold a space or a comma (`Copenhagen:NYK62 10`, `Copenhagen:4,5PRF4.09`), and in a third item it matched only 2 bond ISINs GNW filed as `Luxembourg :XS…`.
           - none: PRN's RSS (no ticker field), a GNW walk id and a carried request (no index row behind either), an `Index` request. Yahoo's committed sitemap carries no `news:stock_tickers` (0 of 8 rows); a Yahoo row that carried one would be named in its own lane.
         - Reader: `HostQueue::requeue` → `push_document`.
         - PRN's RSS lists a story first, so dedup keeps the RSS listing; when PRN's sitemap names a ticker for a story this run already queued, `attempt_once` returns its story in `Attempted::promoted` and `HostQueue::promote` moves the queued RSS follow-up from `unnamed` to the back of `named`, before the sitemap's own new follow-ups join. Its request, `listed_date`, `listed_by`, story and cap count stay the RSS's; a walk id or a carried request of a promoted story is not moved.
         - The lane order only: the cap is still counted at `pop`, so which host's follow-ups the cap cuts is unchanged; inside a lane the unnamed ones are cut first.
         - Rejected: a priority read by `pop` across lanes: it would move one host's turn ahead of another's, which round-robin by host (§10) rules out.
         - Tests: `named_follow_ups_go_first_in_listing_order_and_every_other_request_keeps_its_place`, `a_later_listing_naming_a_ticker_promotes_a_queued_story_and_nothing_else`, `a_stopped_lane_defers_its_named_follow_ups_first` (`news_provider::collect`); `a_prn_sitemap_row_naming_stock_tickers_marks_its_follow_up_and_nothing_else_does` (real `sitemap_p1_1200.xml`, 2 of 3 rows named), `a_gnw_item_with_a_stock_domain_category_names_a_ticker_and_an_isin_alone_does_not`, `a_stock_category_counts_behind_another_and_never_under_a_namespace_prefix`, `a_stock_category_holding_only_whitespace_names_no_ticker` (real `rssfeed_0936_3_items.xml`, each edited in one item), `a_walk_id_a_carried_request_and_a_planned_index_name_no_ticker`; through `collect`: `a_committed_hosts_run_asks_its_hosts_round_robin` (Lilly's RSS follow-up promoted by the sitemap's `NYSE:LLY`), `a_story_the_sitemap_promotes_is_asked_before_the_sitemaps_own_ticker_named_release` (promote before requeue in `collect`), `a_readmitted_canada_newswire_is_collected_after_the_committed_files_robots_refresh` (HKEX's `HongKong:0388` first), `a_story_queued_by_this_run_counts_held_only_once_the_run_asked_it` (the promoted story asked ahead of the cap, `held` 1).

         - `newsvault-collect.timer`: one `OnCalendar=*-*-* HH:MM:00 UTC` per `SLOTS` entry, 31; `AccuracySec=1s`; no `RandomizedDelaySec`, no `Persistent=`, so a missed slot is not run late.

         - `--mount type=bind`, which refuses a run whose host path is missing. Rejected: `--volume`: it creates a missing host path as a root-owned directory (docs.docker.com, bind mounts), so a skipped install step left a `feed-contact` directory every run fails on (`io_failed`) and the user cannot remove.

         - `newsvault-roster.timer` (`*-*-* 01:20:00 UTC`, `AccuracySec=1s`, no `Persistent=`) and `.service` (2026-11-23): `roster fetch`; the collect's NTP check, lock and container flags, its contact file included (`the_collect_and_refresh_units_share_one_lock_and_one_container_shape`); no `SuccessExitStatus`, so exit 8 fails the unit; `TimeoutStartSec=180`, SEC's 30 s patience × 2 requests + 120 s; its result through `newsvault-unit-result roster`. Placement and tests: §10, "The roster".
         - The store lock is S7-D10's separate scheduler lock: the store's own lease already refuses a second writer (exit 7, `lease_held`); the outer lock decides before a container starts. Rejected: `flock --wait`; a waiting collect spends its own window.
         - `newsvault-watchdog.timer` (`*-*-* *:50:00 UTC`, hourly) and `.service`, running `deploy/systemd/newsvault-watchdog` installed as `~/.local/lib/bellwether/newsvault-watchdog`: `ledger --at <now> --from <yesterday> --to <today> --expected-runs 31 --check --format prometheus` in the image, the store bind-mounted `readonly`, `--network none`, written to `.newsvault.prom.<pid>` in `NEWSVAULT_TEXTFILE_DIR` and renamed to `newsvault.prom` for the ledger's exits 0, 1 and 8; any other exit leaves the last file, so the staleness alert fires. `--expected-runs 31`: a day with no run file states no expected count, so without it a day no run reached raised no `runs_below_expected`.
           - Incident 2026-11-23, read on production 2026-11-24 (read-only): every hourly run from about 17:50Z exited 2 with `error: disk I/O error: Error code 6410: disk I/O error`; 6410 is `SQLITE_IOERR_GETTEMPPATH`: SQLite wanted a temporary file and this container, `--read-only` with no `--tmpfs`, holds no writable directory.
           - Trigger: volume. 2026-11-23 was the first full weekday: 2,347 attempts and 2,134 new items in one day. `ledger` sorts every attempt of the store, not the asked days: `grouped_attempts`' `GROUP BY` is `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY` (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, SQLite 3.54.0, 2026-11-24), and a sort past the sorter's memory, `cache_size` pages, goes to a file.
           - Reproduced on production 2026-11-24, by hand: the same command with `--tmpfs /tmp` added exits 1 with a finding.
           - Effect: `newsvault.prom` was not rewritten; `NewsvaultWatchdogStale` fired; the 11 alerts that read the watchdog's families (the table below, `NewsvaultCollectStale` to `NewsvaultRowsZero`) read the last good file for about 15 h.
           - Fix 2026-11-24: `temp_store = MEMORY` on every connection (§8 row T1); no wrapper or unit changed; not deployed.
           - Rejected: `--tmpfs /tmp` on the watchdog and backup containers, the two without one: a fix per wrapper, each a file to install on the VPS, and a command run by hand in a `--read-only` container stays exposed. The 16 MiB of the five containers that have one caps a temporary file where the pragma's limit is the container's memory; a temporary file past 16 MiB was not produced.
           - Memory of the pragma: the peak of `ledger --format json` with and without it, the largest of three runs each, 2026-11-24, `/usr/bin/time -l` on macOS, release build, system SQLite 3.54.0; the store is the ledger fixture plus copies of one attempt with no item, built by row T1's `ledger` test, so a production row is wider. 860,014 is about a year at 2,347 attempts a day:

             | attempts | `commit.sqlite3` | peak footprint, default | peak footprint, `MEMORY` | max RSS, default | max RSS, `MEMORY` |
             |---|---|---|---|---|---|
             | 23,484 | 7.5 MiB | 24.1 MiB | 26.7 MiB | 30.5 MiB | 33.2 MiB |
             | 120,014 | 38.2 MiB | 79.2 MiB | 72.9 MiB | 84.7 MiB | 94.3 MiB |
             | 860,014 | 273.6 MiB | 380.2 MiB | 423.2 MiB | 435.2 MiB | 540.2 MiB |

             - Cost of the pragma at 860,014: 105.0 MiB of RSS, 24% over the default, and 43.0 MiB of footprint.
             - RSS per attempt between 120,014 and 860,014: 0.617 KiB with the pragma, 0.485 KiB without.
             - `ledger` reads every attempt opened up to `--at`, whatever days are asked (`cmd_ledger.rs`, the reads `WHERE opened_at <= ?1`), so the hourly watchdog's peak grows with the store's history with or without the pragma.
             - Linear extrapolation, not measured: 10 times the volume for a year, 8.57 M attempts, is about 5.0 GiB of RSS with the pragma and 4.0 GiB without.
             - No container in `deploy/systemd/` sets `--memory` (2026-11-24), so the limit is the host's RAM.
             - Not built: `ledger`'s attempt reads bounded to the asked days; `--memory` on the watchdog's container.
             - Not read: the VPS's free memory, and the peak of `cut`, `items`, `publish` and `roster show` on a production store.
           - Signals: `NewsvaultWatchdogStale` is the only alert on a failing watchdog. The unit has no `ExecStopPost` result line, unlike collect, backup, roster and shadow, so no `newsvault_unit_result_success{unit="watchdog"}` exists and no failed-unit rule could fire.
           - Sooner, not built: `newsvault-unit-result watchdog` and a failed-unit rule would fire at the evaluation after the first failed run, about 3,600 s before the 7,200 s staleness, and carry the exit status; a run of the image's `ledger` in a `--read-only` container over a full day's volume would have failed before the deploy.

Rejected: a generic default path: the first install's directory was not the old default, and a path in a template reads as a fact about a machine.
       - Metrics: `newsvault ledger --format prometheus`, schema `newsvault.prom/1`, on stdout for the exits 0, 1 and 8 as JSON is; `cmd_ledger::PROMETHEUS_FAMILIES` lists the families. Rejected: a shell step converting the JSON with `jq`: the image holds no `jq`, and the conversion would be untested code beside the tested renderer.
       - Per-day families are labelled `source`, `run_date` and `days_ago` (0 today, 1 yesterday, from `--at`'s UTC date), so a rule can read yesterday's closed day apart from today's running one.
       - Each per-day rule is `max without(days_ago) (…)`, so one day's alert is labelled by `run_date` and keeps its labels across UTC midnight. Rejected: alerts labelled `days_ago`: at the 00:50 read one event resolved as `days_ago="0"` and fired again as `days_ago="1"`, a second notification its silence did not match (promtool v3.15.1, PR #54 review, 2026-11-18).
       - Alerts, `deploy/prometheus/newsvault.rules.yml`; severities `critical` and `warning` are read by no route on the VPS ("Alerting" below):

         | alert | expr | severity | construction |
         |---|---|---|---|
         | `NewsvaultWatchdogStale` | `(time() - max(newsvault_ledger_at_timestamp_seconds{schema="newsvault.prom/1"})) > 7200`, or the series absent | critical | 2 × the watchdog's 3,600 s |
         | `NewsvaultCollectStale` | `newsvault_collect_last_asked_age_seconds > 10800` | critical | 2 × the longest poll period, 5,400 s: more than one slot missed |
         | `NewsvaultNeverAsked` | no request age while a read exists | critical | — |
         | `NewsvaultLedgerIncomplete` | `newsvault_ledger_complete == 0` | warning | ledger exit 8 |
         | `NewsvaultHostHeld` | `newsvault_deferred_host_held > 0` | critical | S7-D8 |
         | `NewsvaultDeferredExpired` | `newsvault_carried_expired > 0` | critical | S7-D8 |
         | `NewsvaultWalkRangeUnreadPersistent` | `newsvault_walk_range_unread_polls >= 2` | critical | a manual poll inside a slot reads one (§11.2's GNW frontier bullets); a changed link shape makes every scheduled poll one |
         | `NewsvaultHoldsCapped` | `newsvault_holds_capped > 0` | critical | S7-D7 |
         | `NewsvaultWallTimeOverBound`, `NewsvaultHostBusyOverBound` | the finding's count `> 0` | warning | S7-D11, owner 2026-11-18 |
         | `NewsvaultRunsMissed` | `runs_below_expected` with `days_ago="1"` | warning | today's count is short until its last slot |
         | `NewsvaultRowsZero` | `rows_committed_zero_against_vendor_rows` `> 0` | warning | §8 row R16 |
         | `NewsvaultCollectFailed` (PR 7) | the collect unit's last `SERVICE_RESULT` not `success`, or its exit status neither 0 nor 8 | critical | S7-D8; never on exit 8 |
         | `NewsvaultBackupStale` (PR 7) | `(time() - newsvault_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds) > 174690`, or the series absent | critical | 2 × the backup's daily 86,400 s + its `TimeoutStartSec` 1,800 s + systemd's 90 s stop timeout: the stamp is the run's start and appears after its scan. Rejected: 172,800 alone: one missed day fired while the next run wrote its copy (`promtool`, 2026-11-18) |
         | `NewsvaultBackupFailed` (PR 7) | the backup unit's last `SERVICE_RESULT` not `success` | warning | exit 8: the copy is in and scanned, and old copies were not deleted, the second scan failed, or a pack is lost, altered or has no whole manifest, or the store could not give a blob the log names (§10, N1, "Packs"); any other exit: no copy that day, stale fires a day later |
         | `NewsvaultRosterFailed` (2026-11-23) | the roster unit's last `SERVICE_RESULT` not `success` | critical | a failed fetch, exit 8 included, is a roster day lost (§10, "The roster") |
         | `NewsvaultRosterMissed` (2026-11-23) | `(time() - newsvault_unit_result_timestamp_seconds{unit="roster"}) > 86670`, or the series absent | critical | the daily 86,400 s + the roster's `TimeoutStartSec` 180 s + systemd's 90 s stop timeout: the stamp is written when a run ends; `the_roster_missed_threshold_is_one_daily_interval_plus_one_runs_bound`; since this rule `newsvault_unit_result_timestamp_seconds` is read by an alert |

         - An alert on a day's count fires while that day is in the two-day range, up to about 48 h after the event; a silence on its `run_date` acknowledges it.
         - No alert reads the findings `holds_a_failure` (any failed attempt, a 404 included) and `coverage_incomplete` (EDGAR, not deployed); both still reach `newsvault_check_findings`.
       - Kubernetes, `deploy/k8s/newsvault-collect.yaml`, not deployed: a PVC and two CronJobs, `0 2,5,8,11-22 * * *` and `30 0,3,6,9,11-21,23 * * *`, `timeZone: Etc/UTC`, whose union is `SLOTS` (one cron line cannot hold 31 slots); `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, `startingDeadlineSeconds: 60`, `activeDeadlineSeconds: 2790`, `backoffLimit: 0`, `restartPolicy: Never`; the contact from key `contact` of Secret `bellwether-feed-contact` (`items` names it), created by hand: `kubectl create secret generic bellwether-feed-contact --from-file=contact=<file>`.
         - Exit 8 as success: `podFailurePolicy` cannot do it; its actions are `FailJob`, `FailIndex`, `Ignore` and `Count`, and `Ignore` starts a replacement pod, a second run in the slot; `successPolicy` reads only succeeded indexes of an Indexed Job. So the pod's shell maps 8 to 0, the twin of `SuccessExitStatus=8`, under `tini -g` so a SIGTERM reaches newsvault; `podFailurePolicy` names exits 2, 4 and 7 `FailJob`, so the Job's condition names the code.
         - Two CronJobs share no `concurrencyPolicy`: on one node, a run past its next slot meets the store lease and exits 7, as two systemd starts cannot (a timer elapsing on an active unit starts nothing). On several nodes the `ReadWriteOnce` claim cannot attach to a second node, so that pod waits in `ContainerCreating` until `activeDeadlineSeconds`.

       - `newsvault snapshot --out <file>` (`cmd_snapshot`): takes the store's lease read-only (`store::hold_lease_to_copy`; `flock` needs no write access, so the store stays a read-only mount), opens the commit log read-only, copies every page in one `sqlite3_backup_step(-1)`, runs `PRAGMA quick_check` on the copy and renames it from `.<name>.partial`. Envelope `newsvault.snapshot/1`: `store`, `out`, `user_version`, `bytes`, `dry_run`, `changed`. `--dry-run` checks the store, the lease and `--out`.
         - One step, because a step of N pages restarts whenever another connection commits (SQLite's backup docs), so a busy store may never finish.
         - Rejected: `VACUUM INTO`, which rebuilds every b-tree instead of copying pages; the host's `sqlite3` 3.45.1 `.backup`: N1's table.

         | condition | code | exit |
         |---|---|---|
         | no `commit.sqlite3` in the store; `--out`'s directory absent | `input_absent` | 4 |
         | `--out` exists | `invalid_argument` | 2 |
         | a writer holds the lease; a writer outside it keeps the log locked past 30 s | `lease_held` (retryable) | 7 |
         | the copy is `SQLITE_CORRUPT` or `quick_check` answers other than `ok` | `input_unparseable` | 2 |
         | any other SQLite or filesystem failure, among them a hot `commit.sqlite3-journal` a killed collect left, which a read-only mount cannot roll back ("attempt to write a readonly database", measured 2026-11-18, Mac, directory mode 555; the next collect rolls it back), and a WAL store (§6) | `io_failed` | 2 |

         - The time, a construction: each slot holds the lock at most its start + `TimeoutStartSec` (2,790 s) + systemd's default stop timeout (90 s); the longest gap that leaves before the next slot is 2,520 s, after each 90-min slot and after 22:00. Of those gaps, the one after 22:00 (22:48 to 23:30) takes the copy right after the US session; 22:55 + 1,800 s + 90 s = 23:26:30.
         - `--nonblock`: a backup that meets a run (a manual refresh, a hung collect) exits 7 and `NewsvaultBackupFailed` fires. Rejected: waiting: a backup that started late would still hold the lock at 23:30 and cost a collect slot.

What the three files hold, their order and what a killed run leaves: §10, N1, "Packs".
         - Every container call is `docker exec -u www-data <container>`, the writes alone with `-i`; no `--privileged`, no root, no `sudo`. With `<dir>` = `$NEXTCLOUD_DATA/$NEXTCLOUD_USER/files/$NEXTCLOUD_FOLDER`, in order, the pack and its manifest only on a night `blobs pack` wrote one:

           | step | call | on failure |
           |---|---|---|
           | folder | `mkdir -p -- <dir>`, after the snapshot | exit 7 |
           | read | two `sh -c` calls in `<dir>`: `<pack> <wc -c> <sha256sum>` for each `bellwether-vault-blobs-*.tar`, then one `tar -cf -` of every `bellwether-vault-blobs-*.tar.manifest`, unpacked on the host into the work directory; they are `blobs pack`'s `--have` and `--manifests` | exit 7 |
           | pack | `newsvault blobs pack --log /out/commit.sqlite3 --have /out/have --manifests /out/manifests --out /out/<pack>`, a `docker run` | its own 2 or 4 ends the run; its 8 is the run's exit after the retention |
           | write | `sh -c 'cat >"$1" && wc -c <"$1"' sh <dir>/.<name>.part`, the file on stdin: the pack, its manifest, the log archive | exit 7 |
           | size | each printed byte count against its file's size | exit 7, nothing renamed |
           | rename | `mv -- <dir>/.<name>.part <dir>/<name>`, one `rename(2)` in one directory, in the same order, after all three are written | exit 7 |
           | scan | `php occ files:scan --path=$NEXTCLOUD_USER/files/$NEXTCLOUD_FOLDER` | exit 7 only when `occ` itself fails: `files:scan` exits 0 on an unknown user, a path it cannot find and every other error it catches (`apps/files/lib/Command/Scan.php`, stable30 to 32 and master, read 2026-11-18) |
           | lookup | `php occ info:file /$NEXTCLOUD_USER/files/$NEXTCLOUD_FOLDER/<name>` for each file renamed; it exits 1 on a file Nextcloud does not know (`core/Command/Info/File.php`, same reading) | exit 7 |
           | metric | §10, N1, "Packs" | exit 2 |
           | list | `ls -1A -- <dir>` | exit 8, nothing deleted |
           | delete | one `rm -f --` of the oldest log archives beyond 7 and of every `.part` a killed run left of a log archive, a pack or a manifest; also on a night `blobs pack` exits 8 | exit 8 |
           | scan again | only after a delete, so Nextcloud drops the deleted files; an error it catches still exits 0, and the next run's first scan of the folder drops them (`Scanner::handleChildren`, not run) | exit 8 |

Rejected: "the listing holds the copy": a copy whose name sorts after it (a clock that ran ahead, a file put there by hand) made the new copy the oldest; the PR #56 review's run against the stub with seven `20990101`-to-`20990107` copies exited 0 with only those seven left. Names match the shape whole (`grep -x`).
         - Rejected: renaming into place before the size check: a short write would sit under the final name. Rejected: the staging suffix `.partial`: Nextcloud's scanner indexes it, so a killed run's full-size file entered the index at the next run's first scan; `Scanner::isPartialFile` skips `.part` (stable32, read 2026-11-18).

## 12. `filingvault` — the annual-report archive as the filings context (owner decisions 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25; design, no code)

- Status of every line of §12: design, no code. No §8 row is claimed from it; §12.7 lists the gates planned.
- Owner decision 2026-11-24 (layout B): the archive of annual reports is the memo's `filingvault` context (memo §3). It gets its own crate and its own store (lock, schema version, backup, coverage ledger, timers) inside the `vault` deployable and image. The mechanics every archive needs sit in a shared crate and reach it by PRs that move code with no behaviour change. `newsvault` keeps the news context (sources, lanes, the 31-run schedule, the cut for `derive`). The roster stays in `newsvault` until `marketvault` is built.
- Owner rule 2026-11-24: code goes in the component that owns the responsibility; every piece has exactly one home, with the reason (§12.1).
- Accepted by the owner 2026-11-24: the whole report is the header page, the whole primary document and the listed text exhibits, with no graphics and no XBRL; free public sources only; one nightly run; pace 500 ms; a stop after 3 consecutive traffic 403 answers; a 64 MiB document limit; one contact for every SEC request; collection by form, never by a roster filter; "newest" ordered by period first.
- Owner decisions 2026-11-25: `FV-Q1` to `FV-Q11` (§12.11). A line below that rests on one names it.
- Not yet assigned: the person who labels the 200 documents (`FV-Q5`, §12.4).
- Units: MB = 10^6 B, GB = 10^9 B, MiB = 2^20 B. "Probe 1" and "probe 2" are §12.10's.

### 12.1 What lives where and why

Their tests are `services/newsvault/tests/deploy.rs` and `monitoring.rs`, 2,715 and 1,175 lines (`wc -l`, 2026-11-25).

  - Known debt (§12.6): the tests of deployable-level files sit in one context's crate.
- Why the shared mechanics are two crates and not one:

  - store mechanics are inside the service crate `services/newsvault`, which a sibling context may not link; only they need a new crate.
- Owner decision 2026-11-25 (`FV-Q1`): transport, pace and the send gate stay in `news-provider`, where they are shared today; `vault-core` holds store mechanics only.
  - It narrows the decision of 2026-11-24, which named the three among what moves into the shared crate.
  - Rejected: moving them into `vault-core`. Symptom, counted 2026-11-24 at `ea59293`: `wire`, `budget`, `clock`, `ledger` and `request` are 2,186 source and 3,265 test lines (lines before and after each file's first `#[cfg(test)]`) and cannot move in parts (`wire` needs `ledger::SendPermit`, `ledger` needs `wire::RawResponse`, and row R4 needs the permit and `Wire::send` in one crate); 87 lines of this document name `news-provider` or `news_provider::` (`grep -c`); `CLIENT_ALLOWLIST` and the clock scan's `SEAM_CRATE` name the crate.
  - A `vault-core` that declares `ureq` could not later serve `modelgate` without `modelgate` linking a second HTTP owner (row R4).
- Size of the store-mechanics move, counted the same way: `services/newsvault/src` is 14,401 source lines; `blobs.rs` 811, `robots.rs` 432, `contact.rs` 127; the opener, the lease and the log copy about 164 (counted from item ranges, not from a diff); 1,534 lines, 10.7%.
- `filingvault` writes its own schema, sink, document door, coverage reader, run record and CLI. The news versions key on `story_id` and `Published` and carry news-only columns (`hosts_version`, `held`, `listing_unusable`, `relisted_compared`, `robots_disallowed`, `continuity`, `boundary_*`, `listed_by`).

**What `filingvault` meets in the conversation core's types (read at `7b6e6f7`, 2026-11-25).**

| `Request.target_window` | the window asked | `<kind>/<target>`: the only field that can carry five kinds | stored as `kind` and `target` |

| `Request.hosts_version`, `extract_version`, `listed_date`, `names_ticker` | admission, extraction and lane order of news | `None`, `None`, `None`, `false` | dropped |
